questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Root hairs are developed from the ...
questions.explanation: Root hairs are tubular outgrowths of single cells of the root epidermis (piliferous layer).

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: In a dicot leaf, guard cells differ from other epidermal cells because they
questions.explanation: Guard cells are the only epidermal cells that contain chloroplasts.

questions.stem: Herbs differ from shrubs because they
questions.explanation: Herbs have soft, non-woody stems while shrubs are woody.

questions.stem: If an organic compound has its Hydrogen : Oxygen ratio as 2:1, it is likely to be
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y, i.e. hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2:1 as in water.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements are necessary for the formation of chlorophyll in a plant?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is part of the chlorophyll molecule and iron is needed for its synthesis; lack of either causes chlorosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true of mammalian erythrocytes?
options: They appear yellow when looked at singly
The cells are more numerous than leucocytes
questions.explanation: Mature mammalian red blood cells lose their nuclei.

questions.stem: In woody plants, gases and water vapour are transported across the stems by the
questions.explanation: Medullary rays run radially across the stem and allow lateral movement of gases and water.

questions.stem: The kidneys of all vertebrates act as osmoregulators. This means that they
options: keep the composition of the plasma constant
control the volume of blood entering the kidneys
decrease the osmotic pressure of blood
increase the osmotic pressure of blood
questions.explanation: Osmoregulation by the kidneys keeps the water and salt composition (osmotic concentration) of the blood plasma constant.

questions.stem: The movement of part of a plant in response to external stimulus of no particular direction is
questions.explanation: Nastic movements are responses of plant parts to non-directional stimuli (e.g. closing of Mimosa leaves).

questions.stem: The part of the mammalian brain responsible for maintaining balance is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscular movement and maintains balance and posture.

questions.stem: In the onion bulb, food is stored in the
questions.explanation: Food is stored in the fleshy leaf bases (inner scale leaves); the outer scale leaves are dry and protective.

questions.stem: What type of fruit is formed from a single flower having several free carpels?
questions.explanation: An aggregate fruit develops from one flower with an apocarpous (free-carpel) gynoecium.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases is NOT caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Maize rust is a fungal disease (Puccinia); the others are viral.

questions.stem: A centipede differs from a millipede by its
options: paired legs on each abdominal segment
questions.explanation: Centipedes have a pair of poison claws behind the head; millipedes do not.

questions.stem: An organism having one pair of identical genes is
questions.explanation: Having two identical alleles for a trait makes an organism homozygous.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Plants which can survive in places where the water supply is limited are
questions.explanation: Xerophytes are adapted to dry habitats with limited water.

questions.stem: Banana, plantain and pineapple can be grouped together because they
questions.explanation: All three are propagated vegetatively by suckers.

questions.stem: One disease NOT caused directly by bacteria is
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium.

questions.stem: In what order do the following structures develop during the metamorphosis of the toad? 1. External gills 2. Internal gills 3. Forelimbs 4. Hindlimbs 5. Mouth.
questions.explanation: The tadpole first has external gills, then the mouth opens, internal gills form, hindlimbs appear and finally forelimbs.

questions.stem: The dental formula i 3/3: c 1/1: pm 4/4: m 2/3 = 42 represents that of a
questions.explanation: This 42-tooth formula with canines and carnassial premolars is that of the dog.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true of insectivorous plants?
options: They obtain part of their food by trapping and feeding on insects
They attract insects simply because of pollination
They can grow in soils poor in nitrogenous salts
They can supplement the nitrogen supply by feeding on insects
Examples include butterworts, sundews and pitcher plants
questions.explanation: Insectivorous plants attract insects to trap and digest them for nitrogen, not merely for pollination.

questions.stem: Which of these worms is beneficial to man?
questions.explanation: Earthworms aerate and enrich the soil; the others are parasites.

questions.stem: Starting from the skull end, the vertebrae are arranged in the following order:
options: axis, atlas, cervical, thoracic and lumbar
atlas, cervical, axis, thoracic and lumbar
atlas, axis, thoracic, cervical and lumbar
atlas, axis, cervical, thoracic and lumbar
atlas, thoracic, cervical, axis and lumbar
questions.explanation: The atlas is the first vertebra, followed by the axis, the remaining cervical, then thoracic and lumbar vertebrae.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases could be exclusively associated with a river basin?
questions.explanation: Onchocerciasis (river blindness) is spread by Simulium blackflies that breed in fast-flowing rivers.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents the evolutionary sequence in these plants? 1. Flowering plants, 2. Ferns, 3. Mosses, 4. Algae, 5. Conifers.
questions.explanation: Plants evolved from algae to mosses, ferns, conifers (gymnosperms) and then flowering plants.

questions.stem: Which of the following will NOT allow osmosis to take place?
questions.explanation: Polythene is impermeable to water, so it cannot act as a semi-permeable membrane.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements on the mammalian circulatory system is NOT true?
options: Blood in the pulmonary artery is richer in oxygen content than blood in the pulmonary vein
The blood in the hepatic portal vein is the richest in food substances
Blood flow is controlled by valves in the veins
Arteries are generally thicker and larger than veins
Fibrin helps in the formation of blood clot
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs; the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood back.

questions.stem: In a positive phototropic response of a coleoptile, the region of greatest curvature is brought about by the
options: movement of auxins away from the region of curvature
even distribution of auxins in all parts of the coleoptile
inhibition of growth by auxins in the region of smaller curvature
concentration of auxins in the region of curvature
absence of auxins in the coleoptile
questions.explanation: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, where cells elongate more, producing the curvature towards light.

questions.stem: The tuber of cassava is NOT a stem tuber because it
options: has other structures that could be called roots
has a bark over its stored food
questions.explanation: Cassava is a root tuber: it lacks nodes with axillary buds (eyes) found on stem tubers.

questions.stem: The function of the ossicles (malleus, incus and stapes) in the mammalian ear is the
questions.explanation: The ossicles transmit and amplify vibrations from the eardrum to the oval window.

questions.stem: Which of the following instruments is used for determining turbidity of water?
questions.explanation: The Secchi disc measures the transparency/turbidity of water.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of monocot plants?
questions.explanation: Monocots generally lack a cambium and so do not undergo secondary thickening.

questions.stem: Which sequence represents the correct order of organisms in a food chain? 1. Toad, 2. Mucuna, 3. Grasshopper, 4. Snake, 5. Hawk.
questions.explanation: Mucuna (producer) is eaten by the grasshopper, which is eaten by the toad, the snake and then the hawk.

questions.stem: In Rhizopus, carbohydrate is stored in the form of
questions.explanation: Fungi such as Rhizopus store carbohydrate as glycogen, not starch.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the rate of transpiration is INCORRECT? It is
options: affected by changes in light intensity
questions.explanation: High humidity reduces the rate of transpiration, so it is not unaffected by humidity.

questions.stem: ‘Jointed skeleton’ is absent in the
questions.explanation: The snail is a mollusc; the others are arthropods with jointed exoskeletons.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the dentition of man is INCORRECT? Man has
options: the same number of teeth on upper and lower jaws
questions.explanation: The adult human formula i 2/2, c 1/1, pm 2/2, m 3/3 gives 12 molars, not six.

questions.stem: When a Spirogyra cell is immersed in a salt solution more concentrated than its cell sap, it
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution the cell loses water by osmosis and becomes plasmolysed.

questions.stem: Urea is produced in the
questions.explanation: Urea is formed in the liver by deamination of excess amino acids (ornithine cycle).

questions.stem: What is the genetic ratio of the F2 generation if members of the F1 generation (from a cross of pure tall and pure short plants) are allowed to self-pollinate?
questions.explanation: Selfing heterozygous Tt plants gives 3 tall : 1 short in the F2.

questions.stem: The path taken by glucose from the ileum to the heart is
options: ileum → hepatic portal vein → hepatic artery → vena cava → heart
ileum → hepatic portal artery → hepatic artery → vena cava → heart
ileum → hepatic portal vein → vena cava → heart
ileum → hepatic vein → vena cava → heart
ileum → hepatic portal vein → hepatic vein → vena cava → heart
questions.explanation: Absorbed glucose goes via the hepatic portal vein to the liver, leaves by the hepatic vein into the vena cava and reaches the heart.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The mouth parts of the housefly are adapted for
questions.explanation: The housefly has a sponging proboscis (labella) used to lap up liquefied food.

questions.stem: The male toad differs from the female by having
questions.explanation: Only male toads have vocal sacs used for croaking during mating.

questions.stem: Mosses, liverworts and ferns can be grouped together because they
questions.explanation: Bryophytes and pteridophytes reproduce by spores and do not produce seeds.

questions.stem: Which of the following invertebrates does NOT possess antennae?
questions.explanation: Spiders (arachnids) have no antennae.

questions.stem: Which of the following is INCORRECT? The prothallus of a fern
options: is green because its cells contain chloroplasts
is attached to the ground by numerous rhizoids
questions.explanation: The prothallus is the small gametophyte; the sporophyte (fern plant) is the dominant generation.

questions.stem: Which of the following cell constituents is NOT common in both plants and animals?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts occur only in plant cells.

questions.stem: The character-producing factors in living organisms are
questions.explanation: Genes are the units (factors) that determine characters.

questions.stem: A mixture of mercurous and mercuric nitrates is added to a food substance. A white precipitate is formed which on gentle heating turns red. The food substance is
questions.explanation: This is Millon’s test, which gives a white precipitate turning red with proteins.

questions.stem: The mammalian organ through which nourishment and oxygen diffuse into a developing embryo is called
questions.explanation: Exchange of food and oxygen between mother and foetus takes place across the placenta.

questions.stem: Osmosis can be defined as the movement of
options: molecules from solution of high concentration to low concentration
molecules from solution of low concentration to high concentration
water from solution of high concentration to low concentration
water across a semi-permeable membrane from solution of low concentration to high concentration
water across a semi-permeable membrane from solution of high concentration to low concentration
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from a dilute (low concentration) solution to a concentrated one.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true of enzymes? They
options: are sensitive to hydrogen ion concentration
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins and are denatured by high temperatures.

questions.stem: The dorsal and anal fins of fish are used for
questions.explanation: The unpaired dorsal and anal fins keep the fish stable, preventing rolling and yawing.

questions.stem: Exoskeleton is NOT found in the
questions.explanation: The earthworm is an annelid with a hydrostatic skeleton; the others are insects with cuticular exoskeletons.

questions.stem: Blood clotting is initiated by
questions.explanation: Platelets release thrombokinase (thromboplastin) which starts the clotting process.

questions.stem: Pepsin is a digestive enzyme which breaks
options: fats into glycerol and fatty acids
questions.explanation: Pepsin in the stomach hydrolyses proteins to peptones (polypeptides).

questions.stem: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Underground stems which grow horizontally through the soil are
questions.explanation: Rhizomes are horizontal underground stems, e.g. ginger.

questions.stem: A man with normal haemoglobin (AA) marries a woman who has sickle-cell haemoglobin (SS). They have a child who has sickle-cell trait. Which of the following genotypes could be associated with the child’s haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: AA × SS gives only AS children, which is the sickle-cell trait (carrier).

questions.stem: In a Biuret test, some protein was mixed with sodium hydroxide solution. Which of the following chemicals should be added to the mixture for a positive result?
questions.explanation: Dilute copper(II) sulphate is added; a violet/purple colour shows protein.

questions.stem: The removal of a man’s pancreas by surgical operation can affect only the digestion of
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains amylase, trypsin and lipase, which digest starch, proteins and fats.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of vertebrae occur in equal numbers in the rabbit, rat and man?
questions.explanation: Almost all mammals have seven cervical vertebrae.

questions.stem: A flowering plant is monoecious if
options: the androecium is found on one plant
the gynoecium and androecium are on the same plant
questions.explanation: A monoecious plant bears both male and female organs on the same plant.

questions.stem: How many nuclei are found in a pollen tube during fertilization?
questions.explanation: The pollen tube contains one tube nucleus and two male (generative) nuclei.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a waste product of plants?
questions.explanation: Cell sap is a solution within the vacuole, not an excretory product; the others are plant wastes.

questions.stem: If an animal is very active and has good muscular control, it is likely to have well-developed
questions.explanation: The cerebellum controls muscular coordination and balance.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following adaptations is NOT concerned with the flight of birds?
questions.explanation: Webbed feet are an adaptation for swimming, not flight.

questions.stem: The transect method can be used in ecology to show the
options: number of plants and animals in a habitat
distribution of organisms along a line
heights of trees in a section of a forest
number of young plants across a forest
questions.explanation: A line transect records how organisms are distributed along a line across a habitat.

questions.stem: Asexual reproduction does NOT occur in
questions.explanation: Ascaris (roundworm) reproduces only sexually; all the organisms in the other groups reproduce asexually.

questions.stem: Fehling’s solution will readily change colour from blue to a reddish colour when it is
options: mixed with sugar solution in the cold
mixed with reducing sugar in the cold
warmed or heated with a complex solution
warmed with a solution of reducing sugar
questions.explanation: Reducing sugars reduce Fehling’s solution to a brick-red precipitate only on heating.

questions.stem: Normally the flow of blood is NEVER from
questions.explanation: Blood flows artery → arterioles → capillaries → venules → veins, never back from arterioles to artery.

questions.stem: Heat produced in tissue respiration in plants is
questions.explanation: Plants do not use respiratory heat to maintain body temperature, so it is lost as waste energy.

questions.stem: The axial skeleton of a mammal does not include the bones of the
questions.explanation: Limb bones belong to the appendicular skeleton.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences represents the process of blood clotting? 1. Fibrin forms a network of threads 2. Red blood cells are caught and a clot is formed 3. Fibrinogen in plasma changes into insoluble fibrin 4. Blood is exposed to air.
questions.explanation: Exposure to air starts clotting; fibrinogen becomes fibrin, which forms a network that traps red cells.

questions.stem: Green plants are important in the ecosystem because they are
questions.explanation: Green plants make food by photosynthesis and are the producers of the ecosystem.

questions.stem: An anemometer is an instrument for measuring
questions.explanation: The anemometer measures wind speed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a pollutant on land or in the air?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is the main natural component of air, not a pollutant.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following groups of factors is completely abiotic?
questions.explanation: Each other group contains a living (biotic) factor: plankton, insect, conifers or bacteria.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists of diseases, their causes, symptoms and transmission is CORRECT?
options: Cholera, virus, severe diarrhoea, infected water
Malaria, protozoan, high fever, contact with infected person
Syphilis, virus, venereal disease, sexual intercourse
Smallpox, virus, skin with blisters, close contact with infected person
Sleeping sickness, bacteria, tiredness, headaches and dozing, tsetse fly bite
questions.explanation: Smallpox is viral and spread by close contact. Cholera is bacterial, malaria spreads by mosquitoes, syphilis is bacterial and sleeping sickness is protozoan.

questions.stem: Erosion can be reduced along a slope by
questions.explanation: Ridges across (along the contour of) the slope slow run-off and reduce erosion.

questions.stem: If a handful of soil is shaken with water and left to settle, the soil particles will settle from light to heavy particles as follows:
questions.explanation: Humus floats on top, then clay, silt, sand and finally stones at the bottom.

questions.stem: Denitrifying bacteria in nature liberate gaseous nitrogen directly from
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria reduce soil nitrates to free nitrogen gas.

questions.stem: Leaching is
options: washing away of humus from the soil surface
reduction of soil aeration by pressure
soil erosion by means other than rainfall
loss of organic matter due to exposure to direct sunlight
washing out of chalk and limestone from upper layers of soil by heavy rains
questions.explanation: Leaching is the downward washing of soluble minerals (such as lime) out of the upper soil by percolating rain water.

questions.stem: The process of soil erosion is usually from
questions.explanation: Erosion starts as sheet erosion, develops into rills and then into gullies.

questions.stem: In Spirogyra, the pyrenoid
options: makes the plant slimy to touch
questions.explanation: Pyrenoids on the chloroplast are centres of starch formation and storage.

questions.stem: In which of the following groups of animals are flagella and cilia found?
questions.explanation: Flagella (e.g. Euglena) and cilia (e.g. Paramecium) are locomotory organelles of protozoa.

questions.stem: Which of the following is seed bearing?
questions.explanation: The whistling pine (Casuarina) is a seed plant; mosses, algae, liverworts and ferns reproduce by spores.

questions.stem: Each of the following is an arthropod EXCEPT the
questions.explanation: The snail is a mollusc.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: In fish the sense organs which detect movements in the water are located within the
questions.explanation: The lateral line system detects vibrations and water movements.

questions.stem: Euglena is an autotrophic organism because it
questions.explanation: Autotrophs make their own food; Euglena photosynthesises with its chloroplasts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of Mucor? It
questions.explanation: Mucor is a fungus and has no chlorophyll.

questions.stem: Bryophytes are different from flowering plants because they
questions.explanation: Bryophytes lack xylem and phloem, which all flowering plants possess.

questions.stem: At what stage in the life history of a toad is its mode of breathing similar to that of a fish?
questions.explanation: At the internal gill stage the tadpole passes water over gills covered by an operculum, as a fish does.

questions.stem: In lower plants like mosses, the structure which performs the functions of roots of higher plants is called
questions.explanation: Mosses are anchored and absorb water through rhizoids.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: In an angiosperm leaf, the xylem is
options: in separate bundles from the phloem
questions.explanation: In the vascular bundles of a leaf the xylem lies on the upper (adaxial) side and the phloem below it.

questions.stem: A group of similar cells performing the same function is
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing a common function.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following is common to a dicotyledonous stem and a monocotyledonous root?
questions.explanation: Both the dicot stem and the monocot root have a central pith.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents the sequence of protein hydrolysis? 1. Polypeptides 2. Amino acids 3. Proteins 4. Peptones
questions.explanation: Proteins are broken to peptones, then polypeptides and finally amino acids.

questions.stem: A food substance which produces red colouration with Sudan III contains
questions.explanation: Sudan III stains fats and oils red.

questions.stem: If calcium is deficient in food this may cause
questions.explanation: Calcium is needed for bones and teeth; deficiency causes rickets and stunted growth.

questions.stem: Partially digested food ready to leave the stomach is referred to as
questions.explanation: The acidic, partly digested food leaving the stomach is chyme.

questions.stem: The function of lymph nodes is to
questions.explanation: Lymph nodes filter bacteria and foreign particles from lymph and produce lymphocytes.

questions.stem: The vein which returns blood from the head and arms to the heart is called
questions.explanation: The superior (anterior) vena cava drains the head, neck and arms.

questions.stem: Blood platelets are important because they
questions.explanation: Platelets start the clotting process that leads to thrombin formation.

questions.stem: If a child can receive blood from all donors, he belongs to the blood group
questions.explanation: Group AB has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies and is the universal recipient.

questions.stem: Which of the following events does NOT occur during anaerobic respiration of glucose?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration does release energy, though less than aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: Identify which of the following are characteristics of the vertebrate respiratory surface. 1. Moist 2. Vascularized 3. Semipermeable 4. Freely permeable 5. Dry
questions.explanation: Respiratory surfaces are moist, richly supplied with blood vessels and permeable to gases; they are never dry.

questions.stem: In mammals, the function of the sebaceous gland is to
options: manufacture vitamin D for the skin
questions.explanation: Sebaceous glands secrete sebum, an oily substance that keeps hair and skin supple.

questions.stem: Which of the following organs regulates the amount of amino acids and glucose in the body?
questions.explanation: The liver stores excess glucose as glycogen and deaminates excess amino acids.

questions.stem: The appendicular skeleton is made up of the
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton consists of the pectoral and pelvic girdles and the limbs.

questions.stem: The maize grain is a fruit and not a seed because it
questions.explanation: A fruit develops from the ovary; the maize grain is a caryopsis whose wall is the fused pericarp and testa.

questions.stem: If a flower is protandrous then it
questions.explanation: In protandry the anthers mature before the stigma, which prevents self-pollination.

questions.stem: For pollen to be released in Crotalaria the insect must depress the
questions.explanation: The stamens and style are enclosed in the keel; pressing it down exposes them to the insect.

questions.stem: Irish potato is a
questions.explanation: The Irish potato has nodes with buds (eyes), so it is a stem tuber.

questions.stem: The characters by which an organism is recognized are termed its
questions.explanation: The observable characteristics of an organism are its phenotype.

questions.stem: The hereditary material in a cell is known as
questions.explanation: DNA in the chromosomes carries hereditary information.

questions.stem: A young plant showing yellow leaves is likely to be deficient in
questions.explanation: Magnesium is part of chlorophyll; its deficiency causes chlorosis (yellowing).

questions.stem: Germination which results in the cotyledons being brought above ground is called
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination the hypocotyl elongates and carries the cotyledons above the soil.

questions.stem: The mammalian endocrine system is responsible for
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands secrete hormones, which bring about chemical co-ordination.

questions.stem: An old man is likely to be long-sighted because age affects the
questions.explanation: With age the ciliary muscles weaken and the lens loses elasticity, so near objects cannot be focused (presbyopia).

questions.stem: In a mammal, stimulus is transferred from the receptor to the central nervous system through the
questions.explanation: Sensory (afferent) neurons carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: A relationship between living organisms which is of mutual benefit is
questions.explanation: Symbiosis (mutualism) benefits both partners.

questions.stem: Which of the following food chains is in the correct sequence?
questions.explanation: A food chain starts with the producer (weeds), then tadpoles, beetles that eat tadpoles, fish and man.

questions.stem: The primary and secondary hosts respectively of bilharzia are
questions.explanation: Schistosoma matures in man (primary host); the freshwater snail is the secondary (intermediate) host.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT caused by bacteria?
questions.explanation: Onchocerciasis is caused by a filarial worm (Onchocerca volvulus).

questions.stem: Tsetse fly is harmful to man because it is associated with the spread of
questions.explanation: The tsetse fly transmits Trypanosoma, which causes sleeping sickness.

questions.stem: Soil erosion CANNOT be controlled by
questions.explanation: Bush burning exposes the soil and increases erosion.

questions.stem: Water retention is highest in soils which are rich in
options: sand, poor in humus and devoid of clay
clay and sand, but poor in humus
clay and humus, but poor in sand
clay, poor in humus and devoid of sand
sand and humus, but poor in clay
questions.explanation: Clay and humus both hold water well, while sand drains it away.

questions.stem: The origin of mineral particles in the soil is
questions.explanation: Mineral particles come from the weathering of parent rock.

questions.stem: Atmospheric nitrogen is directly replenished in nature through
options: the breakdown of ammonium salts in the soil
the activities of nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria convert nitrates to free nitrogen gas, returning it to the atmosphere.

questions.stem: The initial volume of water poured into a bag of dry soil was 50 ml and the amount that drained through was 35 ml. The percentage water content of the fully soaked soil is therefore
Which of the following pairs are fully adapted to terrestrial life?
questions.explanation: Seed plants (angiosperms and conifers) do not need water for fertilization and are fully adapted to land.

questions.stem: Which of these animals is radially symmetrical?
questions.explanation: Hydra, a coelenterate, is radially symmetrical.

questions.stem: Which of the following has cones?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms such as pines bear their seeds in cones.

questions.stem: For effective functioning of a bird’s quill feather, hooks fit on the ridges of the
questions.explanation: The hooklets of the distal barbules catch onto the ridged proximal barbules, keeping the vane intact.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of Spirogyra?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra consists of unbranched filaments.

questions.stem: Incomplete metamorphosis occurs in the
questions.explanation: The grasshopper develops egg → nymph → adult without a pupal stage.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Fishes are cold-blooded because their body temperature is
options: dependent on that of their surroundings
questions.explanation: Poikilotherms have body temperatures that vary with the environment.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: When the original king and queen of termites die, they are replaced by
options: the king and queen of another colony
some adult reproductives from the same colony
some adult workers which are specially fed to breed
developing nymphs nurtured as secondary reproductives
questions.explanation: Nymphs in the colony are fed specially and develop into supplementary (secondary) reproductives.

questions.stem: The male cockroach differs from the female by having
questions.explanation: Only the male has a pair of anal styles; both sexes have cerci.

questions.stem: The fins making up the limbs of the bony fish are
questions.explanation: The paired pectoral and pelvic fins correspond to the limbs of other vertebrates.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: The stem differs from the root in having the xylem and phloem strands
questions.explanation: In stems xylem and phloem lie together on the same radius in each bundle; in roots they alternate.

questions.stem: Oxygen liberated during photosynthesis has been demonstrated to come from
questions.explanation: Isotope (O-18) experiments show the oxygen comes from the photolysis of water.

questions.stem: The main organic substances found in the human body are
questions.explanation: Salts are inorganic; fats, carbohydrates and proteins are organic.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is part of the haem group of haemoglobin.

questions.stem: The severe deficiency of vitamin C leads to
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes scurvy.

questions.stem: In addition to the high calories derived from fats and oils, they are
questions.explanation: Fat stored under the skin insulates the body against heat loss.

questions.stem: The extract from a food substance reacting with sodium hydroxide and copper sulphate solutions will produce violet to purple coloration if
questions.explanation: This is the Biuret test for protein.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: The three important organs that are situated close to the stomach are
questions.explanation: The gall bladder, pancreas and spleen lie close to the stomach; the kidneys are against the back body wall.

questions.stem: Evidence that a tooth is a living part of the mammalian body can be found within the
questions.explanation: The pulp cavity contains blood vessels and nerves, showing the tooth is living.

questions.stem: Blood circulation in a mammal is said to be double because
options: it passes twice through the heart in the complete circuit
it moves in both arteries and veins
it circulates in both the heart and other organs
the heart contains auricles and ventricles
questions.explanation: Blood passes through the heart twice (pulmonary and systemic circuits) in one complete circulation.

questions.stem: Which is the correct order of water loss from the leaf? 1. Mesophyll 2. Veins 3. Substomatal cavity 4. Stomata
questions.explanation: Water moves from the veins (xylem) into the mesophyll, evaporates into the substomatal cavity and diffuses out through the stomata.

questions.stem: The aperture between the left auricle and the left ventricle is guarded by the
questions.explanation: The bicuspid (mitral) valve guards the left atrioventricular opening.

questions.stem: A major limitation in the use of the potometer for measuring the rate of transpiration is that
options: it is made of breakable glass material
it measures the rate of water intake
it measures the rate of water loss through the stem only
the movement of the air bubble in the potometer cannot be timed accurately
questions.explanation: The potometer measures water uptake, which is not exactly equal to the water lost by transpiration.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not correct with respect to inhalation in mammals?
options: Pressure of the thoracic cavity decreases
questions.explanation: During inhalation the diaphragm contracts and flattens (is lowered), not raised.

questions.stem: The equation that can be used to summarize the process of anaerobic breakdown of sugar is
questions.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation converts glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide with release of a little energy, without oxygen.

questions.stem: Deamination occurs in the
questions.explanation: Excess amino acids are deaminated in the liver.

questions.stem: In the mammalian skin, melanin and keratin are contained in the
questions.explanation: The Malpighian (germinative) layer of the epidermis contains melanin and produces keratinised cells.

questions.stem: Two main distinguishing features of the cervical vertebra are the presence of
options: short neural spine and vertebrarterial canal
questions.explanation: Cervical vertebrae have a short neural spine and vertebrarterial canals in their transverse processes; the centrum is small.

questions.stem: Nastic movement is
questions.explanation: Nastic movements are responses to non-directional stimuli.

questions.stem: Gestation in mammals is the period
options: between the formation of the foetus and birth
of development from zygote to birth
before the formation of the zygote
questions.explanation: Gestation is the period from fertilization (zygote) to birth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of discontinuous variation?
questions.explanation: Handedness falls into distinct categories; the others vary continuously.

questions.stem: The hormone which regulates the amount of glucose in the blood is called
questions.explanation: Insulin from the islets of Langerhans lowers blood glucose.

questions.stem: An instrument that can be used to demonstrate phototropism and geotropism in plants is the
questions.explanation: The klinostat rotates the plant to cancel one-sided stimuli, used as a control in tropism experiments.

questions.stem: In an ecosystem, animals which feed directly on plants are called
questions.explanation: Herbivores are primary consumers.

questions.stem: In an agricultural ecosystem, the biotic component consists of
questions.explanation: Only living things are biotic; temperature, humidity, water and soil are abiotic.

questions.stem: Which of these diseases CANNOT be prevented by immunization?
questions.explanation: There is no vaccine against onchocerciasis; polio, TB (BCG) and cholera vaccines exist.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following ecological factors are common to both terrestrial and aquatic habitats?
questions.explanation: Salinity and tides are aquatic factors and altitude/humidity terrestrial; rainfall, temperature, light and wind affect both.

questions.stem: In a community, bacteria and fungi are referred to as
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi break down dead matter and are decomposers.

questions.stem: The swollen shoot disease of cocoa tree is caused by a
questions.explanation: Cocoa swollen shoot is a viral disease spread by mealybugs.

questions.stem: A large percentage of tropical soils tend to be acidic because they
options: lose a high proportion of their organic matter to running water
lose lime and potash from the top soil through rain action
questions.explanation: Heavy rainfall leaches basic ions (lime and potash) from the topsoil, leaving it acidic.

questions.stem: The following are methods of soil conservation EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Grazing (especially overgrazing) exposes soil; it is not a conservation method.

questions.stem: Samples of different soil types are packed in glass tubes whose lower ends are plugged with cotton wool. If these tubes are suspended in a trough of water, water will rise highest after a few hours in
questions.explanation: Clay has the finest pores and so the greatest capillarity.

questions.stem: The function of endoplasmic reticulum is
options: digestion and destruction of foreign bodies
questions.explanation: The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of membranes that transports materials within the cell; protein synthesis itself is done by ribosomes.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: An organism found on a bare rock surface has features of algae and fungi. The organism is
questions.explanation: A lichen is a symbiotic association of an alga and a fungus and is a pioneer on bare rock.

questions.stem: In a plant exhibiting alternation of generations, the diploid multicellular stage is known as
questions.explanation: The diploid generation produces spores and is the sporophyte.

questions.stem: A characteristic that distinguishes bryophytes from flowering plants is the
options: possession of true stems and leaves
ability to grow in moist habitats
questions.explanation: Bryophytes have no xylem or phloem.

questions.stem: A good example of a diploblastic organism is
questions.explanation: Coelenterates such as Hydra have two body layers (ectoderm and endoderm).

questions.stem: The function of the clitellum in the earthworm is to
questions.explanation: The clitellum secretes the cocoon in which eggs are laid.

questions.stem: The crayfish is an arthropod because
options: its body consists of a cephalothorax and an abdomen
it has a pair each of antennae and antennules
every segment of its body carries a pair of appendages
its body is covered with an exoskeleton made of chitin
questions.explanation: A chitinous exoskeleton (with jointed appendages) is the defining feature of arthropods; the other features are specific to crustaceans.

questions.stem: The hypha of Rhizopus is said to be coenocytic because it
questions.explanation: A coenocytic hypha has no septa, so many nuclei share one cytoplasm.

questions.stem: In most true ferns sporangia are grouped into
questions.explanation: Fern sporangia are clustered in sori on the underside of the fronds.

questions.stem: In the reproduction of mosses, water is essential because
options: the male gametes must swim to fertilize the ovum
questions.explanation: Moss antherozoids swim through a film of water to reach the archegonium.

questions.stem: In tapeworm, the two structures that run through the length of the body are the
options: nerve cord and the excretory duct
sperm duct and the nerve cord
genital pore and the excretory duct
sperm duct and the genital pore
questions.explanation: Longitudinal nerve cords and excretory canals run the whole length of the strobila; reproductive organs are repeated in each proglottid.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of snails?
options: Soft unsegmented body in a mantle
questions.explanation: The snail’s shell is calcareous; a chitinous exoskeleton is an arthropod feature.

questions.stem: In the life history of a butterfly, destruction of crops is caused by the
questions.explanation: The caterpillar (larva) has biting mouthparts and feeds on leaves.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: The correct sequence of tissues in the anatomy of a young dicotyledonous stem from the inside to the outside is
options: pith, phloem, cambium, xylem, parenchyma, collenchyma and epidermis
xylem, phloem, cambium, cortex, endodermis, collenchyma and epidermis
pith, xylem, cambium, phloem, collenchyma, parenchyma and epidermis
phloem, xylem, cambium, cortex, endodermis, collenchyma and epidermis
questions.explanation: Only this option has the correct central order pith → xylem → cambium → phloem, followed by the cortex tissues and the epidermis.

questions.stem: Secondary thickening is initiated in a dicotyledonous stem by the
questions.explanation: The cambium divides to form secondary xylem and phloem.

questions.stem: In demonstrating the importance of mineral elements in plants, the culture bottle must be darkened to
options: prevent algal growth in culture solution
questions.explanation: Excluding light stops algae growing in the solution and using up the minerals.

questions.stem: The vitamin which is important in the formation of the retina pigments is
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is used to make rhodopsin (visual purple) in the retina.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists of organs is directly involved in nutrition?
options: Oesophagus, bronchus, stomach, pancreas and anus
Spleen, pharynx, duodenum, jejunum and rectum
Teeth, oesophagus, ileum, lungs and large intestine
Salivary gland, liver, stomach, villi and colon
questions.explanation: All of these are parts of the digestive system; the other lists include the bronchus, spleen or lungs.

questions.stem: In the standard experiment to show that oxygen is given off during photosynthesis, sodium bicarbonate is used to
options: supply mineral salts to water plant
questions.explanation: Sodium hydrogencarbonate releases carbon dioxide for the water plant.

questions.stem: One cubic centimetre of lymph is richer than an equal volume of blood in
questions.explanation: Lymph contains many lymphocytes (leucocytes) but no red cells, and less food than blood.

questions.stem: The oxidative part of the respiration process takes place in the
questions.explanation: Aerobic (oxidative) respiration occurs in the mitochondria.

questions.stem: Fatigue of leg muscles may occur after riding many kilometres on a bicycle because of
questions.explanation: With insufficient oxygen the muscles respire anaerobically and accumulate lactic acid, causing fatigue.

questions.stem: The function of the loop of Henle is to
options: concentrate amino acids in the kidney tissue
concentrate sodium chloride in the medulla of the kidney
questions.explanation: The loop of Henle builds up a high salt concentration in the medulla so water can be reabsorbed and urine concentrated.

questions.stem: Sclerenchyma cells are lignified to
questions.explanation: Lignified sclerenchyma fibres give mechanical strength and support.

questions.stem: A flower showing radial symmetry is said to be
questions.explanation: Actinomorphic flowers are radially symmetrical.

questions.stem: A samara differs from a cypsela by having
options: a pericarp fused with the seed coat
some hairy outgrowths on the pericarp
questions.explanation: A samara has its pericarp extended into a wing; a cypsela bears a hairy pappus.

questions.stem: The plantain reproduces asexually by
questions.explanation: Plantain and banana produce suckers from the underground stem.

questions.stem: Growth can best be determined in a population of Spirogyra by measuring the
options: rate of photosynthesis in the population
questions.explanation: Dry weight (dry mass) is the most reliable measure of growth.

questions.stem: Most cells in higher animals retain their power of division EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Mature nerve cells do not divide.

questions.stem: A severe deficiency of thyroxine results in
questions.explanation: Thyroxine deficiency in childhood causes cretinism.

questions.stem: The growth of a coleoptile towards a unilateral light source is due to
questions.explanation: Auxin collects on the shaded side, which grows faster and bends the coleoptile towards light.

questions.stem: The sequence of ear ossicles from the fenestra ovalis is
questions.explanation: The stapes sits in the oval window, joined to the incus and then the malleus on the eardrum.

questions.stem: The centre for controlling body temperature in the brain is the
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the thermoregulatory centre.

questions.stem: Unlike auxins, gibberellins
options: induce the formation of adventitious roots
do not affect leaf and fruit abscission
questions.explanation: Auxins promote rooting, control abscission and are used as herbicides; gibberellins do none of these but strongly stimulate stem elongation.

questions.stem: A gene which expresses itself only in the homozygous condition is
questions.explanation: A recessive allele shows its effect only when homozygous.

questions.stem: An example of monohybrid inheritance in man is
questions.explanation: Albinism is controlled by a single recessive gene.

questions.stem: If a plant homozygous for round and yellow (RR;YY) is crossed with a wrinkled green type (rr;yy), all of the resulting seeds will be
questions.explanation: All F1 are RrYy and show the dominant traits, round and yellow.

questions.stem: The ratio of carriers to sicklers in the F1 generation derived from a parental cross of two carriers of haemoglobin S gene is
questions.explanation: AS × AS gives 1 AA : 2 AS : 1 SS, so carriers : sicklers = 2 : 1.

questions.stem: In which of the following crosses will all the female offspring be colour blind?
options: colour blind mother × colour blind father
questions.explanation: Daughters receive an X from each parent; only if both parents’ X chromosomes carry the allele are all daughters colour blind.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following relates to edaphic factors?
options: The structure of the earth’s surface
The influence of living organisms on each other
The influence of soils on plants and animals
questions.explanation: Edaphic factors are soil factors.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Epiphytes growing on the branches of trees provide an example of the relationship known as
questions.explanation: Epiphytes benefit from support while the tree is not harmed: commensalism.

questions.stem: Poliomyelitis is an infectious disease caused by
questions.explanation: Polio is caused by the poliovirus.

questions.stem: One of the functions of UNICEF is to
options: prevent disease outbreak by administering vaccines
improve the health and nutrition of children and nursing mothers
questions.explanation: UNICEF (the UN Children’s Fund) works to improve the health and nutrition of children and mothers.

questions.stem: Nitrifying bacteria are important because they
questions.explanation: Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter oxidise ammonium compounds to nitrites and nitrates.

questions.stem: The process by which lime is added to clay soils is known as
questions.explanation: Lime causes fine clay particles to clump together (flocculate), improving soil structure.

questions.stem: The function of ribosomes in cells is
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is common to Euglena, white blood cell and Amoeba?
questions.explanation: All three are cells bounded by a cell membrane; none has a cell wall or cilia.

questions.stem: The term ‘Thallophyta’ refers to
questions.explanation: Thallophytes have an undifferentiated thallus body: algae and fungi.

questions.stem: The following organisms are hermaphrodites EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Schistosoma has separate male and female worms.

questions.stem: Parasitic forms are NOT found among
questions.explanation: Flatworms and nematodes include many parasites and annelids include leeches; molluscs are essentially free-living.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of organisms represents the correct trend from simple to complex structural organization? 1. Mollusca 2. Platyhelminthes 3. Nematoda 4. Protozoa
questions.explanation: Complexity increases from Protozoa to flatworms, roundworms and then molluscs.

questions.stem: Spirogyra, Euglena and Chlamydomonas share many characteristics EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Euglena and Chlamydomonas swim with flagella, but Spirogyra is non-motile.

questions.stem: The prothallus of a fern is equivalent to the gametophyte generation of a moss because it
questions.explanation: The gametophyte is the generation that bears the sex organs (antheridia and archegonia).

questions.stem: What is the function of trichocysts in Paramecium?
questions.explanation: Trichocysts are discharged threads used for defence and anchorage.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The long and coiled intestine of a young tadpole is an adaptation to its
questions.explanation: Young tadpoles feed on plant matter, which needs a long gut for digestion.

questions.stem: Lung books are used for respiration in
questions.explanation: Spiders breathe with lung books.

questions.stem: Insects and millipedes have many features in common EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Millipedes have simple eyes (ocelli), not compound eyes.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The major function of the swim-bladder in fishes is
questions.explanation: The swim-bladder adjusts the fish’s density to give buoyancy.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following statements gives the BEST description of bark?
options: Cork-like tissues found only in stems
Brown tissues never found in primary growth
questions.explanation: Bark is all the tissues outside the vascular cambium (phloem, cortex, cork).

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: In the transverse section of the leaf of maize, vascular bundles are arranged in
questions.explanation: The parallel veins of a monocot leaf appear as a single row of bundles in transverse section.

questions.stem: If an animal has a diastema, it would NOT possess
questions.explanation: The diastema is the gap occurring where the canines would be in herbivores such as the rabbit.

questions.stem: If the gall bladder of a mammal is damaged, which of the following will be most seriously affected?
questions.explanation: The gall bladder stores bile, which emulsifies fats for digestion.

questions.stem: Which of the following will be first digested if ingested at the same time?
questions.explanation: Digestion of starch begins in the mouth with salivary amylase, before protein (stomach) and fat (duodenum).

questions.stem: If the phloem of a healthy plant is killed by heat treatment, the
options: upward movement of salts will cease
food manufactured in the leaves will accumulate
leaves of the plant will become yellow
questions.explanation: Phloem translocates manufactured food; when it is killed the food accumulates in the leaves.

questions.stem: In the mammalian respiratory system, exchange of gases occurs in the
questions.explanation: Gaseous exchange takes place across the thin walls of the alveoli.

questions.stem: In the kidney the malpighian corpuscle is located in the
questions.explanation: Malpighian corpuscles (glomerulus and Bowman’s capsule) lie in the cortex.

questions.stem: The skin, through the sweat glands, functions as
questions.explanation: Sweat removes water, salts and some urea, so the skin acts as an excretory organ.

questions.stem: Parenchyma cells serve as supporting tissue when they
questions.explanation: Turgid parenchyma cells press against one another and give support.

questions.stem: Taxism differs from tropism because
options: it is a response to multi-directional stimuli
part of the organism is affected
questions.explanation: A taxis is movement of the whole organism; a tropism is growth movement of part of a plant.

questions.stem: A dry dehiscent fruit which breaks up into one-seeded parts is a
questions.explanation: A schizocarp splits into one-seeded mericarps.

questions.stem: Air spaces are characteristic of seeds or fruits dispersed by
questions.explanation: Air spaces make water-dispersed fruits (e.g. coconut) buoyant.

questions.stem: In vegetative propagation, which of the following requires part of another plant to develop?
questions.explanation: A scion must be grafted onto a stock (another plant) to grow.

questions.stem: Which of these plant groups are normally propagated by asexual means?
questions.explanation: All four are grown from vegetative parts (suckers, tubers, crowns, stem cuttings); rubber, orange and coffee are usually raised from seed.

questions.stem: In a mammal, the placenta performs functions similar to those of the
questions.explanation: The placenta supplies oxygen (lungs), removes wastes (kidneys) and supplies food (digestive system) to the foetus.

questions.stem: The radicle of a bean seedling grows most rapidly in the region
questions.explanation: The zone of elongation lies just behind (above) the root tip.

questions.stem: The main function of the choroid is
options: supply of nutrients to tissues of the eye
questions.explanation: The choroid is rich in blood vessels that nourish the eye (and is pigmented to absorb light).

questions.stem: What part of the central nervous system is concerned with answering an examination question?
questions.explanation: Thinking, memory and voluntary actions are controlled by the cerebrum.

questions.stem: If a dark-skinned woman (Bb) marries an albino man (bb) and they have four children, how many of the children will be dark-skinned?
questions.explanation: Bb × bb gives 1 Bb : 1 bb, so on average 2 of 4 children are dark-skinned.

questions.stem: A red-coloured flower when crossed with a white-coloured one produced pink flowers. This is an example of
questions.explanation: The intermediate pink colour shows incomplete dominance (blending).

questions.stem: The turbidity of a pond can be measured using the
questions.explanation: The Secchi disc measures turbidity/transparency of water.

questions.stem: If an organism obtains its food by means of haustoria, it is said to be
questions.explanation: Haustoria penetrate host tissues to absorb food, as in parasites like dodder.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following relationships involves only one organism?
questions.explanation: A saprophyte feeds on dead organic matter; the other relationships involve two living organisms.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following has the greatest influence on the distribution of animals in marine and fresh water habitats?
questions.explanation: Salinity determines whether an animal can live in sea or fresh water.

questions.stem: Which of these groups of animals is likely to be found in fresh water?
options: Blood worm, pond skater and scorpion
Blood worm, pond skater and dragonfly larva
Pond skater, scorpion and dragonfly larva
Pond skater, blood worm and ant-lion
questions.explanation: Scorpions and ant-lions are terrestrial; blood worms, pond skaters and dragonfly nymphs live in fresh water.

questions.stem: One of the characteristics of plants in the savanna is the
options: production of seedlings on mother plant
questions.explanation: Thick corky bark protects savanna trees against fire and drought.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases can be contracted in areas with fast flowing rivers?
questions.explanation: Simulium blackflies, vectors of river blindness, breed in fast-flowing rivers.

questions.stem: The mineral nutrient that is most bound to the soil is
questions.explanation: Phosphate is strongly fixed by soil particles and is the least mobile nutrient.

questions.stem: The mineral nutrient that easily gets leached out of the soil is
questions.explanation: Nitrate is very soluble and is not held by soil colloids, so it is easily leached.

questions.stem: Most commercial fertilizers are rich in salts of
questions.explanation: Compound (NPK) fertilizers supply the major nutrients nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

questions.stem: When a virus is placed in a non-living medium it
questions.explanation: Outside living cells viruses are inert and can be crystallized.

questions.stem: A multinucleate body without internal cell boundaries is characteristic of
questions.explanation: Fungal hyphae such as those of Mucor are coenocytic (no cross walls, many nuclei).

questions.stem: Double fertilization is a unique feature of
questions.explanation: Only flowering plants have double fertilization (zygote and endosperm nucleus).

questions.stem: Mineral salts can be absorbed into the roots by
questions.explanation: Ions enter root cells by diffusion and by active transport using energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common characteristic of crustaceans?
options: Possession of a pair of antennae
Possession of two pairs of antennae
Each segment has a pair of walking legs
Four pairs of walking legs on the cephalothorax
questions.explanation: Crustaceans have two pairs of antennae (antennules and antennae).

questions.stem: The body of a snail is divided into head,
questions.explanation: A snail’s body consists of head, foot and visceral mass (hump).

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: In a dicotyledonous stem, each companion cell is found beside the
questions.explanation: Companion cells lie alongside sieve tube elements in the phloem.

questions.stem: If a healthy potted plant is continuously kept in dim light
options: the rate of respiration may equal that of photosynthesis
more carbon dioxide and water are taken in
the volume of oxygen released increases
questions.explanation: At low light the plant may reach its compensation point, where photosynthesis equals respiration.

questions.stem: The pancreatic juice contains the enzymes amylopsin,
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains amylopsin (amylase), steapsin (lipase) and trypsinogen.

questions.stem: Aged erythrocytes are destroyed in the
questions.explanation: Old red cells are broken down in the liver (and spleen).

questions.stem: The seedlings in a rice field were found to have thin lanky growth with reddish leaves and poor root development. This is because the soil lacks
questions.explanation: Phosphorus deficiency causes poor root growth, stunted spindly plants and reddish-purple leaves.

questions.stem: There will be agglutination when the
options: Group A serum mixes with Group A erythrocytes
Group A serum mixes with Group B erythrocytes
Group AB serum mixes with Group O erythrocytes
Group B serum mixes with Group B erythrocytes
questions.explanation: Group A serum contains anti-B antibodies, which clump group B red cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the function of lymph?
options: Transports nutrients and oxygen from blood capillaries to the cells
Distributes heat uniformly round the body
Conveys amino acids and glucose from the small intestine to the liver
questions.explanation: Lymph (tissue fluid) bathes the cells and carries nutrients and oxygen from the capillaries to them.

questions.stem: The lumbar vertebra when compared with a thoracic vertebra has a
questions.explanation: Lumbar vertebrae bear much body weight and have large, thick centra and long transverse processes.

questions.stem: Wind-pollinated flowers usually have
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers have long styles with large feathery stigmas hanging outside the flower; pollen is smooth.

questions.stem: The components of castor oil seed and the maize grain are similar EXCEPT for the
questions.explanation: Castor is a dicot (two cotyledons) and maize a monocot (one).

questions.stem: A corm differs from a bulb in that
options: its stem is the main food storage organ
it has a flattened disc-shaped stem
buds are absent in the axils of the leaves
questions.explanation: A corm stores food in a swollen stem, while a bulb stores it in fleshy leaves.

questions.stem: Exponential increase in the population of an organism is a characteristic feature of
questions.explanation: Each division doubles the number of cells, giving exponential growth.

questions.stem: The irreversible life process by which new protoplasm is added to increase the size and weight of an organism can be termed
questions.explanation: Growth is an irreversible increase in size and dry mass through synthesis of new protoplasm.

questions.stem: Fruit enlargement can be induced by spraying young ovary with
questions.explanation: Auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins promote growth; abscisic acid and ethylene are inhibitors/ripening hormones.

questions.stem: A fundamental similarity between nervous and hormonal systems is that both
options: shed chemicals into the blood stream
questions.explanation: Hormones are chemicals, and nerve impulses cross synapses by chemical transmitters.

questions.stem: The region that controls most of the unconscious processes of a mammalian body is the
questions.explanation: The medulla controls involuntary activities such as breathing and heartbeat.

questions.stem: During cell division, the two strands of chromosomes are joined at a point called
questions.explanation: Sister chromatids are held together at the centromere.

questions.stem: When the two alleles present in an organism are of the same type, the genotype is described as
questions.explanation: Identical alleles make the genotype homozygous.

questions.stem: If parents with blood groups AB and OO produce six children,
options: three of them will have group B
two of them will have group A
all the offspring will have group O
none of them will have group A
questions.explanation: AB × OO gives AO and BO in a 1:1 ratio, so of six children three are expected to be group B.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sex-linked character?
questions.explanation: The colour-blindness gene is carried on the X chromosome.

questions.stem: In an ecosystem, the LEAST efficient energy transfer link is from
questions.explanation: Plants capture only about 1% of the sunlight falling on them.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Lichen is an example of
questions.explanation: A lichen is a mutualistic association of an alga and a fungus.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A physiological adaptation of plants to the problem of excessive water loss is
options: reduction in the number of stomata
reversal of the normal stomatal rhythm
questions.explanation: Opening stomata at night and closing them by day (reversed rhythm) is a physiological, not structural, adaptation.

questions.stem: Which of the ways of controlling bilharzia can result in pollution?
options: Clearing water weeds on which the snails feed
Preventing contamination of water by infected urine and faeces
Applying chemicals to kill the snails
questions.explanation: Molluscicides added to water can pollute it and harm other organisms.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases can be caused by a bacterium?
questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum; ringworm is fungal, polio viral and malaria protozoan.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a dangerous product of coal burning?
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide from burning coal is toxic and causes acid rain.

questions.stem: 5 g of oven-dried soil was heated in a furnace for 24 hours; after cooling, it weighed 4.8 g. What is the amount of humus in the soil?
questions.explanation: Humus burnt off = 5 − 4.8 = 0.2 g in 5 g, i.e. 0.2/5 × 100 = 4.0 g per 100 g dry soil.

questions.stem: Most irrigated lands often become unproductive in later years because of
questions.explanation: Evaporation of irrigation water leaves salts that accumulate in the soil (salinization).

questions.stem: Farmers practise crop rotation because it
options: allows two crops to be planted at the same time
is an alternative to shifting cultivation
questions.explanation: Rotating crops with different nutrient needs (including legumes) maintains soil fertility.

questions.stem: Viruses are considered to be living organisms because they
options: move from one place to another
questions.explanation: Inside host cells viruses reproduce and pass on their genetic characters, a property of living things.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics is common to Amoeba and Paramecium?
questions.explanation: Both freshwater protozoa have contractile vacuoles for osmoregulation; oral groove, trichocysts and cilia are found only in Paramecium.

questions.stem: Hydra removes undigested food by
options: egesting it through the body surface
questions.explanation: Hydra has a sac-like gut with a single opening, so undigested food leaves through the mouth.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups of invertebrates reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: Coelenterates such as Hydra reproduce asexually by budding.

questions.stem: The algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes are similar in that they
questions.explanation: In all three groups the male gametes must swim in water to reach the egg.

questions.stem: The spores of ferns are dispersed by
questions.explanation: Fern spores are tiny and light and are dispersed by wind (after the annulus flings them out).

questions.stem: In bryophytes, sex organs are produced in the
questions.explanation: The gametophyte (the leafy moss plant) bears the antheridia and archegonia.

questions.stem: Which of the following animals has homodont dentition?
questions.explanation: A lizard’s teeth are all alike (homodont); mammals are heterodont and pigeons have no teeth.

questions.stem: In which of the following does external fertilization take place?
questions.explanation: Toad eggs are fertilized in water outside the female’s body.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: In the tapeworm, the suckers on the scolex are used for
options: sucking the blood of the host
questions.explanation: Suckers (with hooks) anchor the tapeworm to the host’s intestinal wall.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A feature which adapts birds to flight is the possession of
questions.explanation: Hollow, light (pneumatic) bones reduce body weight for flight.

questions.stem: The nephridia in the earthworm form part of the
questions.explanation: Nephridia are the excretory organs of the earthworm.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases is rarely spread by a housefly?
questions.explanation: Yellow fever is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito; houseflies carry gut pathogens mechanically.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following cells is thin-walled and living at maturity?
questions.explanation: Sieve tube elements are living with thin cellulose walls; xylem vessels and sclerenchyma are dead and collenchyma has thickened corners.

questions.stem: The mode of nutrition in which digestion is extracellular is
questions.explanation: Saprophytes secrete enzymes onto dead matter and absorb the digested products.

questions.stem: The first step in the process of photosynthesis is the
questions.explanation: Light first excites (activates) chlorophyll, which then drives the photolysis of water.

questions.stem: The organ which secretes digestive enzymes as well as hormones is the
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes digestive enzymes and the hormones insulin and glucagon.

questions.stem: The villus in the small intestine is significant because it
options: increases the surface area for absorption
increases the surface area for digestion
questions.explanation: Villi greatly increase the surface area for absorption of digested food.

questions.stem: If a ring of bark and phloem is removed from a stem, the
options: movement of food is not affected
movement of mineral salts is hardly affected
questions.explanation: Ringing removes the phloem but leaves the xylem, so water and mineral salts still move up.

questions.stem: Transpiration can be measured with a
questions.explanation: The potometer measures the rate of water uptake as an estimate of transpiration.

questions.stem: Excretory products responsible for the red, purple and blue colours of flowers are called
questions.explanation: Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments giving red, purple and blue colours.

questions.stem: Etiolation is caused by the influence of
questions.explanation: Plants grown in the absence of light become etiolated (pale and lanky).

questions.stem: Muscles are indirectly attached to bones by means of
questions.explanation: Tendons connect muscles to bones; ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.stem: During mammalian embryo development, large amounts of oestrogen and progesterone are produced in the
questions.explanation: During pregnancy the placenta secretes large amounts of oestrogen and progesterone.

questions.stem: Fruits which develop without fertilization are described as
questions.explanation: Parthenocarpic fruits form without fertilization and are usually seedless.

questions.stem: The part of the ear that is concerned with balance is the
questions.explanation: The semicircular canals detect movement of the head and maintain balance.

questions.stem: In an organism where the 2n number of chromosomes is 16, the number of chromosomes in each gamete will be
questions.explanation: Gametes are haploid (n): 16 ÷ 2 = 8.

questions.stem: What would be the result of the first filial generation (F1) and the second filial generation (F2) of a monohybrid cross between pure line normal-winged Drosophila flies and pure line short-winged flies if the gene for the normal wing is dominant?
options: F1 flies all short-winged and F2 flies all normal-winged
F1 flies all normal-winged and F2 flies all short-winged
F1 flies all short-winged and three-quarters of F2 flies are short-winged
F1 flies all normal-winged and three-quarters of F2 flies are normal-winged
questions.explanation: NN × nn gives all Nn (normal) in F1; Nn × Nn gives 3 normal : 1 short in F2.

questions.stem: An individual in the AB blood group is a universal recipient for blood donation because
options: all the red blood cells do not carry antigen
all the red blood cells carry antigen A
all the red blood cells carry antigen B
there are no anti-A and anti-B antibodies in the serum
questions.explanation: With no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, AB plasma does not agglutinate donated red cells of any ABO group.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: In a savanna ecosystem, the abiotic factors include
questions.explanation: Water, temperature and soil are all non-living; the other options include living organisms.

questions.stem: The salinity of a brackish environment
options: increases at the end of the rainy season
questions.explanation: In the dry season less fresh water flows in and evaporation is high, so salinity rises.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Physiological adaptation to very dry conditions in animals is called
questions.explanation: Aestivation is dormancy during hot, dry periods.

questions.stem: Which set of diseases is spread mainly by insect vectors?
questions.explanation: Malaria (mosquito) and river blindness (blackfly) are insect-borne, and cholera germs can be carried by houseflies; the other sets are mainly spread by water, air or contact.

questions.stem: Which of the following constitutes pollution?
questions.explanation: Loud music is noise pollution.

questions.stem: An acidic soil can be improved upon by
questions.explanation: Liming an acid soil neutralises it and flocculates the clay particles, improving the soil.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: What do bacteria in root nodules derive from the host plant?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium gets shelter and carbohydrates from the legume and fixes nitrogen for it.

questions.stem: Free nitrogen is released to the atmosphere by
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria reduce nitrates to free nitrogen gas.

questions.stem: Angiosperms and gymnosperms belong to the plant group known as
questions.explanation: Seed-bearing plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) are spermatophytes.

questions.stem: Which of the following are non-green plants?
questions.explanation: Fungi lack chlorophyll.

questions.stem: Sting cells are normally found in
questions.explanation: Sting cells (cnidoblasts) are characteristic of coelenterates such as Hydra.

questions.stem: Which of the following are differentiated into true roots, stems and leaves?
questions.explanation: Ferns (pteridophytes) have true roots, stems and leaves with vascular tissue.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: To facilitate gaseous exchange, breathing roots have
questions.explanation: Pneumatophores have lenticels through which gases are exchanged.

questions.stem: The annulus of fern sporangium helps in
questions.explanation: The annulus dries, splits the sporangium and flings out the spores.

questions.stem: In the earthworm, the cocoon is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The clitellum secretes the cocoon.

questions.stem: The function of maxillipeds in crayfish is to aid
questions.explanation: Maxillipeds are mouth appendages that handle food.

questions.stem: The respiratory organ in the land snail is the
questions.explanation: The land snail breathes with a lung formed from the vascular mantle (mantle cavity).

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The gill rakers of fishes take part in
questions.explanation: Gill rakers strain food particles and stop them passing over the gill filaments.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: A wide pith with a ring of conducting tissue is characteristic of the root of
questions.explanation: Monocot roots such as maize have a large central pith surrounded by a ring of many xylem and phloem groups.

questions.stem: Which of the following is formed immediately after the first product of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The first product, simple sugar, is quickly converted to starch for storage.

questions.stem: One of the accessory organs of the digestive system is the
questions.explanation: The liver (producing bile) is an accessory digestive organ.

questions.stem: The element common to protein, carbohydrate and lipid is
questions.explanation: All three contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.stem: The crown of the mammalian tooth is covered with
questions.explanation: Enamel covers the crown; cement covers the root.

questions.stem: In living cells, insufficient oxygen may cause a breakdown of glucose into
questions.explanation: In animal cells, anaerobic respiration converts glucose to lactic acid.

questions.stem: Which of the following can bring about the greatest increase in the rate of transpiration?
questions.explanation: Dry air increases the diffusion gradient of water vapour out of the leaf.

questions.stem: In an experiment, a semi-permeable membrane separates water (X) from a sugar solution (Y). The process by which water moves from X to Y through the semi-permeable membrane is called
questions.explanation: Movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane into a more concentrated solution is osmosis.

questions.stem: Fibrinogen and prothrombin play important roles in the
questions.explanation: Prothrombin forms thrombin, which converts fibrinogen to fibrin in clotting.

questions.stem: Deoxygenated blood flows into the right and left lungs through the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a plant excretory product?
questions.explanation: Resins are plant excretory products; cytokinin is a hormone and amino acids are used.

questions.stem: The movement of the whole organism in response to an external stimulus is termed
questions.explanation: A taxis is a directional movement of the whole organism.

questions.stem: Which of the following vertebrae lacks a centrum?
questions.explanation: The atlas has no centrum; it is a ring of bone that pivots on the odontoid process of the axis.

questions.stem: The function of the epididymis in mammals is the
questions.explanation: Sperms mature and are stored in the epididymis.

questions.stem: A collection of achenes formed from several carpels of a flower is
questions.explanation: Fruitlets from the free carpels of one flower form an aggregate fruit.

questions.stem: Epigeal germination can be found in
questions.explanation: Groundnut cotyledons are carried above ground; cereals germinate hypogeally.

questions.stem: A dwarf plant can be stimulated to grow to normal height by the application of
questions.explanation: Gibberellins cause stem elongation and reverse genetic dwarfism.

questions.stem: The greatest contribution to genetic studies was made by
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel founded the science of genetics with his laws of inheritance.

questions.stem: The exchange of genes between homologous chromosomes is called
