questions.explanation: Crossing-over exchanges segments between homologous chromatids during meiosis.

questions.stem: When two heterozygotes mate, the dominant trait will appear in
options: both the F1 and F2 generations
neither the F1 nor F2 generation
questions.explanation: Heterozygous parents show the dominant trait and it reappears (3/4) among their offspring.

questions.stem: Which of the following characters is NOT sex-linked?
questions.explanation: River blindness is an infection caused by a worm, not an inherited sex-linked trait.

questions.stem: Organisms in an ecosystem are usually grouped according to their trophic level as
questions.explanation: Trophic levels are made up of producers and the various consumers.

questions.stem: A food web is more stable than a food chain because
options: it is not easy to destroy
every organism has an alternative food source
questions.explanation: In a web, if one food source declines the consumers can switch to others.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an adaptive feature for arboreal life?
questions.explanation: Teeth are for feeding, not for life in trees; long tails and claws aid climbing and countershading camouflages.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases can be prevented by inoculation?
questions.explanation: BCG vaccine protects against tuberculosis.

questions.stem: Sources of air pollutants are
options: industrial chimneys, burning fossil oils and river dams
sulphur dioxide, acid rain and pesticides
sulphur mines, vehicle exhausts and aerosols
questions.explanation: All three release pollutants into the air; dams and sewage are not air-pollution sources and option B lists pollutants, not sources.

questions.stem: Fertilizers are lost from the soil through
options: sheet erosion, gully erosion and wind erosion
questions.explanation: Soluble fertilizers are lost mainly by leaching, seepage and surface run-off.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Nitrogen-fixing micro-organisms in leguminous plants live symbiotically in the
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives in the root nodules of legumes.

questions.stem: The organelle involved in tissue respiration is the
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria.

questions.stem: A tissue can best be defined as
options: an aggregate of cells performing a similar function
an aggregate of similar cells performing the same function
a mixture of different cell types performing the same function
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells that together perform the same function.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly summarizes the life cycle of a fern plant?
options: Male and female gametangia → zygospore → sporangium → spores
Prothallus → spermatozoid + egg cell → leafy plant → sporangium → spore
questions.explanation: The prothallus produces gametes; fertilization gives the leafy sporophyte, which bears sporangia that release spores.

questions.stem: A major difference between platyhelminthes and coelenterates is that platyhelminthes
questions.explanation: Flatworms are triploblastic (have a mesoderm); coelenterates are diploblastic.

questions.stem: The essential structural difference between Hydra and tapeworm is that while Hydra
options: has a mouth, tapeworm feeds by suckers
questions.explanation: Hydra has two germ layers; the tapeworm has three.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: The flowering period of plants in a habitat is determined by the
questions.explanation: Flowering is controlled by photoperiod, the duration of daylight.

questions.stem: Which of the following insects undergoes incomplete metamorphosis?
questions.explanation: Termites develop egg → nymph → adult without a pupa.

questions.stem: An onion is a bulb because it
options: has a reduced stem and thick fleshy leaves
bears many buds at the nodes
questions.explanation: A bulb is a short disc-like stem with fleshy scale leaves storing food.

questions.stem: Fungi are heterotrophic because they
questions.explanation: Without chlorophyll fungi cannot make their own food.

questions.stem: The major site of photosynthesis in the leaf is the
questions.explanation: Palisade cells contain the most chloroplasts.

questions.stem: 5 cm3 dilute sodium hydroxide solution and 5 cm3 one percent copper sulphate solution are added to a solution of food specimen. The purple colour which is observed shows the presence of
questions.explanation: A purple colour in the Biuret test indicates protein.

questions.stem: The blood vessel which carries blood from the alimentary canal to the liver is the
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries absorbed food from the gut to the liver.

questions.stem: In the absence of oxygen, the pyruvic acid produced during glycolysis is converted to CO2 and
questions.explanation: In anaerobic respiration (as in yeast) pyruvic acid gives ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: The excretory organ in insects is the
questions.explanation: Insects excrete through Malpighian tubules.

questions.stem: The bone of the neck on which the skull rests is known as the
questions.explanation: The atlas (first cervical vertebra) supports the skull.

questions.stem: Which enzymes are contained in the pancreatic juice?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains amylase, lipase and trypsin.

questions.stem: Double fertilization in higher plants is significant because it ensures the
options: formation of a fertile embryo and the endosperm
questions.explanation: One male nucleus fertilises the egg (embryo) and the other fuses with the polar nuclei (endosperm).

questions.stem: In mammalian development, the function of the yolk is to
options: act as the shock-absorber to the foetus
facilitate the process of excretion in the foetus
questions.explanation: Yolk is stored food that nourishes the early embryo.

questions.stem: Hypogeal germination is characterized by the
options: emergence of the plumule out of the ground
provision of nourishment by the endosperm
questions.explanation: In hypogeal germination the epicotyl elongates, leaving the cotyledons in the soil.

questions.stem: Fruits which develop without fertilization of the ovule are
questions.explanation: Parthenocarpic fruits develop without fertilization.

questions.stem: Neurons that receive stimuli from the body or internal organs are called
questions.explanation: Sensory (afferent) neurons carry impulses from receptors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of a climax community?
options: It persists until the environment or climate changes
It changes drastically from one year to the next
It is the first stage in succession
It is made up of the tallest trees and the smallest animals
questions.explanation: A climax community is stable and remains until conditions change.

questions.stem: A population is defined as a collection of similar organisms that
options: are found in the same habitat
questions.explanation: A population is a group of organisms of one species that can interbreed.

questions.stem: In a typical predator food chain involving secondary and tertiary consumers, the organisms become progressively
options: smaller and more numerous along the food chain
equal in number and size along the food chain
larger and fewer along the food chain
parasitized along the food chain as consumers get bigger
questions.explanation: Predators along a food chain are generally larger and fewer in number.

questions.stem: In a pyramid made up of algae, tadpoles, tilapia and sharks, which organism functions as a tertiary consumer?
questions.explanation: Algae (producer) → tadpole (primary) → tilapia (secondary) → shark (tertiary consumer).

questions.stem: Mangrove swamp can be found
options: on a sea shore with flat terrain
where a river meets the sea
on a mud flat near the sea
questions.explanation: Mangrove swamps occur in brackish estuaries, where rivers meet the sea.

questions.stem: Soil with the finest particles is called
questions.explanation: Clay particles are the smallest (less than 0.002 mm).

questions.stem: Malaria symptoms are caused by
options: toxins released into the blood as a result of the destruction of red blood cells
the multiplication of the malarial sporozoites in the liver
the invasion of the red blood cells by the trophozoites
the development of merozoites into gametocytes
questions.explanation: Fever and chills follow the bursting of red cells, which releases toxins into the blood.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the children of a haemophilic man who marries a woman that is not haemophilic and does not carry the trait?
options: All their sons will be haemophilic
All their daughters will be haemophilic
All their daughters will be carriers
All their sons will be carriers
questions.explanation: Daughters receive the father’s affected X and become carriers; sons receive his Y and are normal.

questions.stem: If R and r denote the genes for a character, the offspring of the cross between RR and Rr are
questions.explanation: RR × Rr gives RR, RR, Rr, Rr.

questions.stem: Pawpaw seeds collected from a tree with many desirable agronomic qualities did not give rise to plants of desirable characters as the parent because
options: seeds are not reliable for propagating plants
uncontrolled out-crossing can introduce unwanted variability
vegetative propagation is the best form of reproduction for all crops
seeds were not physiologically mature at harvest
questions.explanation: Open (cross) pollination combines genes from unknown pollen parents, producing variable offspring.

questions.stem: The hereditary material of the cell is
questions.explanation: DNA carries the hereditary information.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: An example of plant adaptation to a xerophytic environment is represented by the development of
options: broad canopy and extensive surface root system
rough leaves and shallow root system
questions.explanation: Succulent water-storing tissues and reduced leaves conserve water.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following factors is LEAST likely to affect the animals living in a fresh water habitat?
questions.explanation: Fresh water has very low and fairly constant salinity.

questions.stem: The theory of natural selection was developed by
questions.explanation: Darwin and Wallace jointly proposed natural selection in 1858.

questions.stem: Fossil records found in sedimentary rocks offer some explanation for the theory of evolution because
options: the deposits have remains of organisms characteristic of when they were formed
different strata have remains of organisms of the same kind
only organisms with strong parts are fossilized
most animal and plant fossils bear little resemblance to present day living specimens
questions.explanation: Each rock layer contains organisms of its own age, showing how life changed over time.

questions.stem: On what structures are the units of inheritance situated?
questions.explanation: Genes are located on chromosomes.

questions.stem: Production of naked seeds is a distinctive feature of the group of plants called
questions.explanation: Conifers (gymnosperms) bear naked seeds not enclosed in an ovary.

questions.stem: In which of these features do bryophytes differ from pteridophytes?
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes have vascular tissue; bryophytes do not.

questions.stem: Which of the following organs or cell components are common to both the sporophyte and the gametophyte of a fern?
questions.explanation: Both the prothallus and the fern plant are green and photosynthetic; rhizoids occur only on the prothallus and roots and leaves only on the sporophyte.

questions.stem: In which of the following organisms does a single cell perform all the functions of movement, nutrition, growth, excretion and photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Euglena is a single motile cell that also photosynthesises; Spirogyra is filamentous and non-motile.

questions.stem: In which of the following organisms would glycogen be stored?
questions.explanation: Animals such as the rat (Rattus) store carbohydrate as glycogen; plants store starch.

questions.stem: The most successful group of animals in terms of diversity of species is
questions.explanation: Arthropods (especially insects) have the greatest number of species.

questions.stem: The spores of Mucor are dispersed by
questions.explanation: Mucor spores are light and dry and dispersed by air currents.

questions.stem: The butterfly is of great economic importance because
options: of its use in scientific studies
it adds to the beauty of the environment
it pollinates flowers of crops and other plants
questions.explanation: Butterflies pollinate flowers, including crop plants.

questions.stem: Manufactured food in plants is transported through the
questions.explanation: The phloem translocates manufactured food.

questions.stem: Osmic acid boiled with a solution of food substance gave a black precipitate. This indicated the presence of
questions.explanation: Osmic acid (osmium tetroxide) stains fats and oils black.

questions.stem: The end products of the digestion of fats and oils in mammals are
questions.explanation: Lipase hydrolyses fats to fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.stem: The main function of blood in mammals is to transport
options: carbon dioxide from lungs to tissues
digested food from all the body tissues
questions.explanation: Blood carries wastes away from tissues to the excretory organs; the other options reverse the true direction of transport.

questions.stem: Members of the phylum Protozoa use the contractile vacuole
questions.explanation: The contractile vacuole expels excess water (osmoregulation).

questions.stem: The response shown by the tips of the root and shoot of a plant to the stimulus of gravity is
questions.explanation: Growth response to gravity is geotropism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct order of the vertebrae along the spinal column?
options: Axis, atlas, thoracic, lumbar, cervical, sacral
Atlas, cervical, axis, thoracic, lumbar, sacral
Atlas, axis, cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral
questions.explanation: From the skull: atlas, axis, other cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The bright colours of the comb and feathers in the peacock are for
questions.explanation: The male’s display attracts the female during courtship.

questions.stem: The main function of the petals of a flower is to
options: protect the flower while still in bud
serve as landing stage for insects
protect the inner parts from desiccation
questions.explanation: Coloured petals attract insect pollinators; sepals protect the bud.

questions.stem: In the mammal, the autonomic nervous system consists of
questions.explanation: The autonomic system has sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.

questions.stem: In a seedling whose cotyledons are carried above the soil, this happens because
options: the epicotyl grows faster than the hypocotyl
the hypocotyl grows faster than the epicotyl
both grow at the same rate
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination the hypocotyl elongates rapidly and lifts the cotyledons above ground.

questions.stem: When it is cold, the blood vessels of the skin
options: dilate to increase the amount of blood flowing to the skin
constrict to reduce the amount of blood flowing to the skin
dilate to reduce the amount of blood flowing to the skin
constrict to increase the amount of blood flowing to the skin
questions.explanation: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to the skin and so reduces heat loss.

questions.stem: Which path does sound entering the human ear follow?
questions.explanation: Vibrations pass from the eardrum through the ossicles to the oval window.

questions.stem: What would happen to a man whose pancreas has been surgically removed?
options: The level of blood sugar would increase
The glycogen content of the liver would increase
questions.explanation: Without insulin from the pancreas, blood glucose rises (diabetes).

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Carnivorous plants are usually found in areas
questions.explanation: Insectivorous plants obtain nitrogen from insects to make up for nitrate-poor soil.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Important abiotic factors which affect all plants and animals in the habitat are
questions.explanation: Temperature and rainfall affect organisms in every habitat; turbidity and salinity apply mainly to water.

questions.stem: At which trophic level would the highest accumulation of a non-biodegradable substance occur?
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable chemicals are concentrated at each step (biomagnification), so the top consumers accumulate most.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Two organisms of different species, living in close association but not dependent on each other are referred to as
questions.explanation: Commensals live together without either depending on or harming the other.

questions.stem: Which of the following instruments is NOT used in measuring abiotic factors in any habitat?
questions.explanation: A microscope is for viewing small organisms, not measuring physical factors.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Plants adapted for life in salty marsh are called
questions.explanation: Halophytes tolerate saline conditions.

questions.stem: Which group of plants would be the first colonizers in an ecological succession changing rocks to soil?
questions.explanation: Lichens are the pioneers on bare rock.

questions.stem: Soil fertility can be conserved and renewed by
options: bush burning to remove unwanted debris
questions.explanation: Crop rotation and cover crops maintain nutrients and protect the soil.

questions.stem: What ecological condition favours the breeding of black flies?
questions.explanation: Simulium (black fly) larvae need well-oxygenated, fast-flowing streams.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide poisons tissues by
questions.explanation: CO binds firmly to haemoglobin (carboxyhaemoglobin), preventing oxygen transport.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of discontinuous variation observed in man?
questions.explanation: A person either can or cannot roll the tongue; no intermediates.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Cold blooded animals are referred to as
questions.explanation: Cold-blooded animals are poikilotherms.

questions.stem: Which of these organisms has lost the pentadactyl limb structure?
questions.explanation: Fish fins are not built on the five-digit (pentadactyl) plan found in tetrapods.

questions.stem: The membrane surrounding the vacuole in a plant cell is called the
questions.explanation: The tonoplast is the membrane that bounds the vacuole of a plant cell.

questions.stem: The smallest living organisms which share the characteristics of both living and non-living matter are
questions.explanation: Viruses reproduce only inside living cells but can be crystallised like non-living matter outside them.

questions.stem: Green plants are distinguished from other living organisms by their ability to
questions.explanation: Green plants are autotrophs: they make their own food by photosynthesis.

questions.stem: The soil swallowed by the earthworm to form the worm cast is ground up in the
questions.explanation: The muscular gizzard of the earthworm grinds the ingested soil and food.

questions.stem: Which is the correct order in an evolutionary sequence for the following plant groups?
options: Bacteria, ferns, algae, mosses, seed plants
Bacteria, ferns, mosses, algae, seed plants
Bacteria, algae, mosses, ferns, seed plants
Bacteria, mosses, algae, ferns, seed plants
questions.explanation: Plant evolution runs from simple to complex: bacteria, algae (thallophytes), mosses (bryophytes), ferns (pteridophytes), then seed plants.

questions.stem: In Amoeba, osmoregulation is carried out by the
questions.explanation: The contractile vacuole collects and expels excess water from Amoeba.

questions.stem: The mouth part of the insect (the cockroach) is adapted for
questions.explanation: The cockroach has mandibles for biting and chewing solid food.

questions.stem: Which of the following combinations differentiates a bony fish from a cartilaginous fish? I Presence of gills. II Absence of gill slits. III Possession of bony skeleton. IV Possession of laterally compressed body. V Possession of dorso-ventrally compressed body.
questions.explanation: Bony fish have gill slits covered by an operculum, a bony skeleton and a laterally compressed body; cartilaginous fish have exposed gill slits and are often dorso-ventrally flattened.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which is the most important adaptation of a bony fish to life in water?
options: The possession of a streamlined shape
The covering of the body by a thin film of slime
The possession of a caudal fin
questions.explanation: A streamlined body reduces water resistance and is the key adaptation for moving through water.

questions.stem: The dental formula i 3/3, c 1/1, pm 4/4, m 2/3 is that of a

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals

questions.stem: The activity of ptyalin is likely to decrease with an increase in the concentration of

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals

questions.stem: The process by which a red blood cell placed in distilled water absorbs water until it bursts and releases its contents into the surroundings is known as
questions.explanation: The bursting of red blood cells in a hypotonic solution is haemolysis.

questions.stem: Which of the following waste products in plants is excreted through the stomata and lenticels?
questions.explanation: Gaseous wastes such as carbon dioxide diffuse out through stomata and lenticels.

questions.stem: In animals, meiosis comes
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces the haploid gametes, so it occurs before fertilization.

questions.stem: The fleshy base of a flower to which the different floral parts are attached is known as
questions.explanation: The thalamus (receptacle) bears all the floral parts.

questions.stem: When a short-sighted person views a distant object without spectacles, the image is formed
questions.explanation: In myopia the eyeball is too long or the lens too strong, so distant images focus in front of the retina.

questions.stem: The part of the brain that controls heart beat and breathing is the
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat and breathing.

questions.explanation: Populations of different species living together in an area form a community.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals

questions.explanation: Fungi (mushroom, Rhizopus) and bacteria are the decomposers.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals

questions.explanation: Grass is eaten by grasshopper, grasshopper by lizard, lizard by snake and snake by hawk.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals

questions.explanation: Numbers decrease up the pyramid, so the top (tertiary) consumers are fewest.

questions.stem: Use the list of biomes below to answer the question. 1. Desert 2. Rain forest 3. Southern Guinea savannah 4. Northern Guinea savannah. A biome with a low annual rainfall, few scattered trees within a dense layer of grasses and found in Kano and Katsina States is
questions.explanation: Of the biomes listed, the northern savanna with low rainfall and scattered trees in grassland fits Kano and Katsina.

questions.stem: Use the list of biomes below to answer the question. 1. Desert 2. Rain forest 3. Southern Guinea savannah 4. Northern Guinea savannah. A biome where small mammals undergo aestivation for long periods is
questions.explanation: In the hot, dry desert small mammals aestivate to survive long dry periods.

questions.stem: Ecological succession ends with the formation of a stable
questions.explanation: Succession ends in a stable climax community.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: In a drought situation, plants suffer from water stress which could result in
questions.explanation: Water is the medium for metabolic reactions, so water stress reduces biochemical activities.

questions.stem: The water-retention capacity of a soil indicates its
questions.explanation: Water retention depends on the fine pores that hold water by capillarity.

questions.stem: People who suck petrol with their mouths run the risk of increasing in their blood the concentration of
questions.explanation: Leaded petrol contains lead compounds, which are absorbed and accumulate in the blood.

questions.stem: People with sickle-cell anaemia have haemoglobin
questions.explanation: Sickle-cell sufferers have genotype SS: homozygous for the recessive haemoglobin S allele.

questions.stem: In the gene locus for eye colour in humans, the allele for brown eyes is dominant over the allele for blue eyes. If a homozygous brown-eyed girl has a brother with blue eyes, what are the likely phenotypes of their parents’ eye colour? (Eye colour is not a sex-linked trait.)
options: Their father has blue eyes and their mother has brown eyes.
Their mother has blue eyes and their father has brown eyes.
questions.explanation: The BB girl needs a B from each parent and the bb boy a b from each, so both parents are Bb, i.e. brown-eyed.

questions.stem: The sex-linked defect in which a very slight cut produces severe bleeding is known as
questions.explanation: Haemophilia is a sex-linked failure of blood clotting.

questions.stem: Breathing root is an adaptation for survival in the
questions.explanation: Mangroves grow in waterlogged, oxygen-poor mud and use breathing roots (pneumatophores).

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Red coloration on the head of a male lizard helps it to
questions.explanation: The red head of the male Agama is a display to attract females.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A phenomenon by which an animal goes into a state of dormancy during the dry season is called
questions.explanation: Dormancy during hot/dry periods is aestivation; hibernation is during cold.

questions.stem: The anatomical evidence usually used in support of an evolutionary relationship among whales, humans, birds and dogs is the possession of
questions.explanation: All have the homologous pentadactyl limb, evidence of common ancestry.

questions.stem: Which of the following does a virus have in common with animal cells?
questions.explanation: A virus is only nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) in a protein coat; it has no nucleus, cytoplasm or glycogen.

questions.stem: Which of the following organelles are likely to be present in cells that are actively respiring and photosynthesizing?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out respiration and chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.

questions.stem: One common characteristic of fungi, algae, mosses and ferns is that they
questions.explanation: All four groups reproduce by spores that are dispersed; fungi lack chlorophyll and only some show conjugation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is transmitted through mosquito bite?
questions.explanation: Filarial worms are transmitted by the Culex mosquito; typhus and plague by lice/fleas, schistosomiasis by water snails.

questions.stem: Which of the following insects lays its eggs in horny, purse-like cases?
questions.explanation: The cockroach lays its eggs in a horny purse-like case called an ootheca.

questions.stem: In which of the following vertebrates does the skin function as a respiratory surface?
questions.explanation: The moist skin of the frog is used for gaseous exchange (cutaneous respiration).

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Birds maintain their body temperature with the help of their
options: veins which transport fluid of constant temperature to all body tissues
questions.explanation: Feathers trap air and insulate the bird’s body.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Secondary thickening in dicotyledonous stem is controlled by the
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium divides to produce secondary xylem and phloem.

questions.stem: 2H2O → 2H2 + O2(g). The equation above represents a part of the light stage of photosynthesis. Which of the following must be present for this reaction to occur?
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water needs light energy absorbed by chlorophyll.

questions.stem: In an experiment to investigate the effect of nitrogen on the growth of plants, the substrate should be a medium of
questions.explanation: Washed sand contains no nutrients, so the nitrogen supplied can be controlled.

questions.stem: Which vitamin plays an important role in blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors such as prothrombin.

questions.stem: The mammalian organ which acts both as a digestive and as an endocrine organ is the
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes digestive juice and the hormones insulin and glucagon.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT involved in the transport of substances in the body?
questions.explanation: Leucocytes (white cells) defend the body; plasma, lymph and red cells transport substances.

questions.stem: The end product of glycolysis in plants and animals is
questions.explanation: Glycolysis breaks glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid.

questions.stem: During respiration, air circulates round plant tissues via the
questions.explanation: Within the plant, gases move through the intercellular air spaces.

questions.stem: The excretory structure in the earthworm is the
questions.explanation: Earthworms excrete through nephridia.

questions.stem: During the bending of the arm, the biceps muscle
options: contracts and the triceps muscle relaxes
relaxes and the triceps muscle contracts
questions.explanation: Biceps and triceps are antagonistic: the biceps contracts to bend (flex) the arm while the triceps relaxes.

questions.stem: When a healthy shoot of a flowering plant is illuminated from one side, auxins accumulate on the
questions.explanation: Auxin moves to the shaded side, which grows faster so the shoot bends towards light.

questions.stem: The term caryopsis is used to describe a fruit in which the
options: seed coat and fruit wall are impermeable
questions.explanation: A caryopsis (e.g. maize grain) is a dry fruit whose pericarp is fused with the testa.

questions.stem: The sex of a foetus is determined during
questions.explanation: Sex is fixed at fertilization by whether the sperm carries an X or a Y chromosome.

questions.stem: Biological growth refers strictly to an increase in the
questions.explanation: True growth is an irreversible increase in the amount of protoplasm (dry mass); size can increase merely by water uptake.

questions.stem: The process of walking is under the control of the part of the brain called
questions.explanation: The cerebellum co-ordinates muscular movement and balance.

questions.stem: The gland directly affecting metabolic rate, growth and development is known as
questions.explanation: Thyroxine from the thyroid gland controls metabolic rate, growth and development.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions is involved in the conduction of the nerve impulse?
questions.explanation: Movement of K+ (with Na+) ions across the axon membrane produces the nerve impulse.

questions.stem: The depth of illumination in a water body can be measured with a
questions.explanation: A Secchi disc is lowered until it disappears to measure light penetration (turbidity).

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In a food chain involving a primary producer, a primary consumer as well as a secondary consumer, the sharing of trophic energy is in the form that the
options: primary consumer has more energy than the primary producer
secondary consumer takes up all the energy contents of the primary consumer
energy is shared equally between the three groups of organisms
secondary consumer gets only a small portion of the energy contained in the primary producer
questions.explanation: Energy is lost at each trophic level, so the secondary consumer receives only a small fraction of the producer’s energy.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In spite of the removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, its amount remains more or less constant because
options: it is produced by green plants during photosynthesis
it is produced during respiration by animals
it is absorbed in ocean water
green plants release it during the day
questions.explanation: Respiration returns carbon dioxide to the air, balancing its removal by photosynthesis.

questions.stem: In a tropical rain forest, non-epiphytic ferns and fern allies occur as
questions.explanation: Ground ferns grow on the dim forest floor as shade-loving species.

questions.stem: Colonization of a bare rock surface is termed
questions.explanation: Succession starting on bare, never-colonised surfaces is primary succession.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a measure for the control of bilharzia?
options: Application of molluscicides in water bodies
Screening windows and doors with mosquito nets
Application of herbicides in water bodies
questions.explanation: Bilharzia (schistosomiasis) is carried by water snails, which are killed with molluscicides.

questions.stem: Some of the diseases caused by bacteria are
questions.explanation: TB, gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial; AIDS and polio are viral.

questions.stem: Environmental pollutants which can work through the media of water, soil and air include
questions.explanation: Sulphur(IV) oxide pollutes air and forms acid rain that acidifies water and soil.

questions.stem: Human height is an example of a feature which depends on both
questions.explanation: Height is a continuous variation influenced by genes and by environment (e.g. nutrition).

questions.stem: A person with type O blood can donate to a patient with type A because the donor’s blood
options: has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies
questions.explanation: Group O red cells carry no A or B antigens, so they are not agglutinated by the recipient’s antibodies.

questions.stem: The DNA molecule is a chain of repeating
questions.explanation: DNA is a polynucleotide: a chain of repeating nucleotides.

questions.stem: The specific number of chromosomes in each somatic cell is represented by
questions.explanation: Somatic (body) cells are diploid, 2N.

questions.stem: A man with blood group A is married to a woman with blood group A. Which of the following group combinations is possible if the family has three children?
questions.explanation: Group A parents (at most AO each) can only have A or O children.

questions.stem: The F1 of a cross between a tall and a dwarf plant was tall. The F1 was advanced to F2. How many of 120 F2 plants will be dwarf?
questions.explanation: F1 Tt x Tt gives 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so 1/4 of 120 = 30 dwarf.

questions.stem: The sons of a colour-blind woman will be colour blind regardless of the state of the father because
options: the egg determines the phenotype of the son
sons inherit the sex chromosomes of their mothers
the father’s sex chromosome is weaker in sons
sex-linked traits express dominance in females
questions.explanation: A son receives his only X chromosome from his mother (the Y comes from the father), so he inherits her X-linked allele.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The slender, long and slightly curved beak of the sunbird is an adaptation for feeding on
questions.explanation: The long curved beak reaches the nectar deep inside flowers.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Scales on reptiles are a feature for
questions.explanation: Dry horny scales reduce water loss, adapting reptiles to land.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The colour of the ventral surface of a fish is lighter than that of the dorsal. This is mainly
questions.explanation: Countershading camouflages the fish from predators above and below.

questions.stem: The least evidence in support of the theory of evolution is provided by the study of
questions.explanation: Comparative anatomy, embryology and geology (fossils) provide evidence of evolution; ecology provides the least.

questions.stem: From which group of animals are the mammals generally believed to have most recently evolved?
questions.explanation: Mammals evolved from mammal-like reptiles.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following is the youngest plant tissue?
questions.explanation: Meristem is the actively dividing tissue from which all other tissues develop.

questions.stem: Viruses differ from all forms of life because they
options: feed on waste products of other organisms
require other living cells to multiply
questions.explanation: Viruses can only multiply inside living host cells.

questions.stem: Annelids differ from nematodes in that they
questions.explanation: Both groups are bilateral, triploblastic and have a complete gut, but only annelids are metamerically segmented.

questions.stem: Which of the following perform similar functions?
questions.explanation: Strobili (cones) and inflorescences both bear the reproductive structures of the plant.

questions.stem: In ferns, the sporophyte
options: is haploid and dependent on the gametophyte
is diploid and independent of the gametophyte
questions.explanation: The fern plant is the diploid sporophyte, which becomes independent of the small gametophyte (prothallus).

questions.stem: The group of insects that undergoes complete metamorphosis is
questions.explanation: Houseflies, beetles and butterflies pass through egg, larva, pupa and adult; cockroaches, grasshoppers and aphids show incomplete metamorphosis.

questions.stem: The nitrogenous substance that is excreted by birds in order to conserve water is
questions.explanation: Uric acid is insoluble and is excreted as a paste with very little water.

questions.stem: In mammals, the exchange of nutrients and metabolic products occurs in the
questions.explanation: Nutrients and wastes are exchanged between blood and cells through the tissue fluid (lymph).

questions.stem: The part of the stomach nearer the gullet is called the
questions.explanation: The cardiac sphincter guards the entrance of the stomach from the oesophagus; the pyloric sphincter is at the exit.

questions.stem: Trace elements are required by plants mainly for the
questions.explanation: Micronutrients such as Fe, Cu, Zn and Mn act in enzyme systems and pigment formation.

questions.stem: A food substance was treated with a few drops of Sudan III solution and a red coloration was obtained. The food contained
questions.explanation: Sudan III stains fats and oils red.

questions.stem: Oozing out of water from the leaves of plants in a humid environment is known as
questions.explanation: Guttation is the loss of liquid water through hydathodes when the air is humid.

questions.stem: The element that is essential for the coagulation of blood is
questions.explanation: Calcium ions are required for the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin during clotting.

questions.stem: Anaerobic respiration differs from aerobic respiration by the production of
options: less amount of energy and water
greater amount of energy and alcohol
less amount of energy and alcohol
greater amount of energy and water
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in yeast/plants releases less energy and produces alcohol (ethanol).

questions.stem: Stomata pores open when there is
options: an increase in the sugar content of guard cells
a decrease in the osmotic concentration of guard cells
a decrease in the sugar content of mesophyll cells
an increase in the sugar content of mesophyll cells
questions.explanation: More sugar in the guard cells lowers their water potential; they absorb water, become turgid and the pore opens.

questions.stem: The process of deamination is essential for the

questions.stem: A band of connective tissue linking two bones in a joint is known as
questions.explanation: Ligaments join bone to bone; tendons join muscle to bone.

questions.stem: The appendicular skeleton is composed of the pectoral girdle,
options: pelvic girdle, fore and hind limbs
lumbar vertebrae, fore and hind limbs
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton is the girdles and the limbs; vertebrae belong to the axial skeleton.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: The companion cells are part of the

questions.stem: In which of the following groups of vertebrates would the largest amount of yolk be found in the egg?

questions.stem: Coconut and oil palm fruits can be grouped as
questions.explanation: Both have a hard stony endocarp around the seed, so they are drupes.

questions.stem: The substance that is responsible for apical dominance in plants is known as

questions.stem: The part of the brain that regulates most biological cycles in humans is
questions.explanation: The pineal body secretes melatonin, which regulates biological rhythms such as sleep cycles.

questions.stem: The ability of the eye to focus on both near and distant objects is termed
questions.explanation: Accommodation is the change in lens shape to focus near and far objects.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: The speed of wind can be measured with an instrument called

questions.stem: Toads and lizards in an ecosystem depend on a limited quantity of food. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Competition between different species for the same limited resource is interspecific.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Adaptive features of plants to desert conditions include
options: thick barks, succulent stems and sunken stomata
thin barks, succulent stems and sunken stomata
thin barks, air floats on stems and sunken stomata
air spaces in tissues, adventitious roots and thick barks
questions.explanation: Thick bark and sunken stomata reduce water loss and succulent stems store water.

questions.stem: The Southern Guinea Savanna differs from the Northern Guinea Savanna in that it has
questions.explanation: The southern Guinea savanna is nearer the forest, with more rainfall and taller grasses.

questions.stem: After a heavy rainfall and the formation of a large pond, the most likely sequence of changes in the vegetation of the pond is
questions.explanation: Succession goes from unicellular algae (Euglena) to filamentous algae (Spirogyra), then rooted floating plants (water lily) and finally land plants (grass) as the pond fills.

questions.stem: In a soil sample, the relative amounts of the different soil particles can best be determined by the process of
questions.explanation: Shaken soil settles in layers by particle size, showing the proportions of gravel, sand, silt and clay.

questions.stem: Which is the most important pollutant of the marine environment in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Crude oil spills from petroleum activities are the main marine pollutant in Nigeria.

questions.stem: One of the most effective ways of controlling guinea worm is by
questions.explanation: Guinea worm is contracted by drinking water containing infected Cyclops, so safe drinking water prevents it.

questions.stem: During binary fission in lower organisms, the nucleus is known to undergo
questions.explanation: Binary fission is asexual; the nucleus divides by mitosis.

questions.stem: The homozygous condition HbS HbS results in sickle cell anaemia whereas HbA HbS has the sickling trait. What is the probability that a couple with the sickling trait will give birth to one normal child?

questions.stem: Which of the following characters is NOT sex-linked?
questions.explanation: Albinism is autosomal; baldness, haemophilia and colour blindness are sex-linked.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: What combination of characters should a prey develop to survive in the environment of its predator?
options: Camouflage, well developed limbs and effective vision
Showy colour, big body and well developed limbs
Camouflage, big body and effective vision
Showy colour, well developed muscles and an acute sense of smell
questions.explanation: Camouflage hides it, good vision detects the predator and well-developed limbs allow escape.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The three classes in a termitarium are
questions.explanation: Termite castes are workers, soldiers and reproductives (king and queen).

questions.stem: Long neck in giraffes is used to illustrate the theory of
questions.explanation: Lamarck explained the giraffe’s long neck by use and disuse with inheritance of acquired characters.

questions.stem: The nucleus is considered the control organelle of a cell because it
options: is bounded by the nuclear membrane
is located at the centre of the cell
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the chromosomes (DNA) that direct all cell activities.

questions.stem: The natural tendency of organisms as they evolve is to
questions.explanation: Evolution proceeds from simple to complex forms with increasing specialisation of structures.

questions.stem: In snails, the hard calcareous shells are secreted by the
questions.explanation: The mantle secretes the calcium carbonate shell of molluscs.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The ability of the cockroach to live in cracks and crevices is enhanced by the possession of
questions.explanation: A flattened body lets the cockroach squeeze into narrow cracks.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The caste of termites that lacks pigmentation is the
questions.explanation: Workers live in the dark nest and are pale (unpigmented); reproductives are pigmented.

questions.stem: The structures that prevent food particles from escaping through the fish gills are called gill
questions.explanation: Gill rakers on the gill arches strain food and protect the filaments.

questions.stem: A distinguishing feature of mammals is the possession of
questions.explanation: Hair (fur) is found only in mammals.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following structures is capable of producing more tissues in the stem of a herbaceous flowering plant?
questions.explanation: The cambium is meristematic and produces new xylem and phloem.

questions.stem: The manufacture of carbohydrates by plants takes place only in
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs wherever chlorophyll is present.

questions.stem: In Millon’s test, when the reagent is added to a protein food item, a white precipitate is produced which turns
questions.explanation: Millon’s reagent gives a white precipitate with protein which turns brick-red on heating.

questions.stem: Unicellular organisms transport essential nutrients directly to all parts of their bodies by the process of diffusion because they have
options: a large volume to surface area ratio
a large surface area to volume ratio
their bodies immersed in the nutrients
their outer membrane made of cellulose
questions.explanation: Small organisms have a large surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion alone is adequate.

questions.stem: The heart of the adult frog consists of
questions.explanation: The amphibian heart is three-chambered: two auricles and one ventricle.

questions.stem: Which of the following movements occur during exhalation?
options: The diaphragm and intercostal muscles relax
The thoracic cavity increases in volume
The diaphragm and intercostal muscles contract
The diaphragm contracts and the intercostal muscles relax
questions.explanation: In exhalation both the diaphragm and the intercostal muscles relax, reducing the volume of the thorax.

questions.stem: In which of the following groups of animals is the Malpighian tubule found?
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a function of the mammalian skeleton?
questions.explanation: The skeleton protects, supports and aids breathing movements, but does not transport materials.

questions.stem: The most reliable estimate of growth is by measuring changes in
questions.explanation: Dry weight measures the actual increase in organic matter, unaffected by water content.

questions.stem: A dry fruit formed from two or more carpels containing several seeds is a
questions.explanation: A capsule develops from a compound ovary of several carpels and contains many seeds.

questions.stem: The outermost embryonic membrane in the mammal is the
questions.explanation: The chorion is the outermost membrane and forms part of the placenta.

questions.stem: The small masses of nervous tissue in which many neurons have their nuclei are called
questions.explanation: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cell bodies.

questions.stem: A group of organisms of different species living in a particular area is described as a
questions.explanation: A community consists of populations of different species in one area.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following is the direct consequence of transferring energy from one trophic level to another?
options: A decrease in the efficiency of energy conversion
An increase in the numbers of resulting individuals
A decrease in the resulting biomass
questions.explanation: Much energy is lost at each transfer, so less biomass can be supported at the next level.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The condition that encourages denitrification is
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria thrive in poorly aerated (waterlogged) soil.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A freshwater plant such as water lily can solve the problem of buoyancy by the possession of
options: thin cell walls of the epidermis
questions.explanation: Aerenchyma contains large air spaces that keep the plant afloat.

questions.stem: The sequence of the biomes in Nigeria from Port Harcourt to Damaturu is

rain forest → Guinea savannah → estuarine → desert
estuarine → Guinea savannah → rain forest → Sahel savannah
rain forest → estuarine → Guinea savannah → desert
questions.explanation: Moving north from the coast: mangrove/estuarine, rain forest, Guinea savanna, then Sahel savanna in the north-east.

questions.stem: Soil micro-organisms are beneficial because of their involvement in
questions.explanation: Soil microbes decompose organic matter and recycle nutrients such as nitrogen.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups of diseases are associated with water? I Onchocerciasis II Schistosomiasis III Dracunculiasis IV Elephantiasis V Taeniasis

questions.stem: One of the ways in which body cells differ from gamete cells is in the
options: number of chromosome pairs they contain
questions.explanation: Body cells are diploid (2n) while gametes are haploid (n).

questions.stem: In blood transfusion, agglutination occurs when
options: white blood cells from two individuals meet
questions.explanation: Clumping occurs when an antigen meets its corresponding antibody (e.g. A antigen with anti-A).

questions.stem: After one week of life, the weights of five chicks of the same sex hatched simultaneously from the eggs of the same hen and fed on the same diet were 45 g, 40 g, 35 g, 33 g and 30 g. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Differences among offspring of the same parents under the same conditions illustrate variation.

questions.stem: The phenotype of an individual can be summed up as the

questions.stem: A sex-linked character cannot be passed on directly from

questions.stem: The biological association that contributes directly to succession in a community is
questions.explanation: Competition leads to the replacement of one group of species by another during succession.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The group of insects that have mouth parts adapted for both piercing and sucking is

questions.stem: In the honey bee colony, the drones are
options: sterile males with reduced mouth parts
sterile males with well-developed mouth parts
fertile males with reduced mouth parts
fertile males with well-developed mouth parts

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

organisms have varying capacities for survival in their habitats
organisms compete for resources and better competitors survive and thrive
habitats allow only organisms that will not have to compete for survival
questions.explanation: Darwin: in the struggle for existence the best-adapted competitors survive and reproduce.

questions.stem: The basic point of impact by changes which produce mutation is the

questions.stem: The habitat of the cysticercus of Taenia solium is

questions.stem: The possession of scales, laying of eggs with shells and bony structure of the head are characteristics shared by
questions.explanation: Birds and reptiles both have scales (birds on legs), shelled eggs and bony skulls.

questions.stem: The group of arthropods that has no antennae is the
questions.explanation: Arachnids (spiders, scorpions) lack antennae.

questions.stem: The structure that is most commonly identified in all living cells under the light microscope is the
questions.explanation: The nucleus is large and clearly visible with the light microscope; ribosomes need the electron microscope.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an organ?
questions.explanation: The liver is made up of several tissues working together; a guard cell is a cell and xylem and blood are tissues.

questions.stem: The division of a body into two equal halves along a longitudinal plane is called
questions.explanation: Bilateral symmetry: only one plane divides the body into two mirror-image halves.

questions.stem: In which of the following organisms does each cell combine the functions of nutrition, reproduction and growth?
questions.explanation: In the filamentous alga Spirogyra each cell photosynthesises, grows and can take part in reproduction.

questions.stem: The key event in the transition of the amphibians from water to land is the
options: replacement of the gills with lungs
questions.explanation: Lungs replace the larval gills, allowing amphibians to breathe air on land.

questions.stem: In plant cells, the chloroplasts are located
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are organelles in the cytoplasm.

questions.stem: In woody stems, gaseous exchange takes place through the
questions.explanation: Lenticels are pores in the bark for gaseous exchange.

questions.stem: Substances manufactured by the leaves are transported to other parts of the plant through the
questions.explanation: Manufactured food is translocated in the sieve tubes of the phloem.

questions.stem: After a meal of yam has been digested, the highest concentration of glucose is to be found in the
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries absorbed food from the intestine to the liver.

questions.stem: The dark reaction of photosynthesis involves
options: fixation of carbon (IV) oxide to give a six-carbon sugar
fixation of carbon (IV) oxide with the help of oxygen
use of carbon (IV) oxide to produce glucose using ATP
fixation of carbon (IV) oxide on chlorophyll using hydrogen
questions.explanation: In the light-independent stage CO2 is reduced to glucose using ATP and hydrogen from the light stage.

questions.stem: Mammals acclimatize to reduced oxygen content at high altitudes by
options: the stimulation of marrow to reduce the amount of erythrocytes produced
increasing the rate at which erythrocytes are destroyed
the stimulation of marrow to produce more erythrocytes
increasing the breakdown of the protein portion of the erythrocytes
questions.explanation: More red blood cells increase the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.

questions.stem: The richest sources of vitamin A are
questions.explanation: Red palm oil and carrots are rich in carotene (provitamin A).

questions.stem: The force that holds water together in the form of a stream within the xylem tube is the
options: cohesion of water molecules to one another by hydrogen bonds
force of gravity attracting the water molecules through the hydrogen bonds
attraction between the water and xylem by osmotic force
normal flow of water from the ground with the help of gravitational force
questions.explanation: Cohesion between water molecules (hydrogen bonding) keeps the water column continuous.

questions.stem: Yellowing of leaves is a symptom associated with deficiency of
questions.explanation: Magnesium (in chlorophyll), nitrogen and iron (needed for chlorophyll formation) deficiencies all cause chlorosis.

questions.stem: The lymphatic system of mammals rejoins the blood circulatory system at the
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct empties lymph into the left subclavian vein.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: In dissection, the rib cage of a mammal has to be opened in order to expose the
questions.explanation: The heart and lungs lie within the rib cage.

questions.stem: Fertilization in humans usually takes place in the
questions.explanation: The ovum is fertilised in the upper part of the oviduct (Fallopian tube).

questions.stem: Insects visit flowers in order to
questions.explanation: Insects come for food (nectar/pollen); pollination is an incidental result.

questions.stem: In epigeal germination, the cotyledons are
options: carried above the ground by the elongating hypocotyl
pulled underground by the elongating hypocotyl
pulled underground by the elongating epicotyl
carried above the ground by the elongating epicotyl
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination the hypocotyl elongates and lifts the cotyledons above the soil.

questions.stem: Bacteria multiply rapidly by means of
questions.explanation: Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission.

questions.stem: The correct sequence for the operation of smell in mammals is
options: dissolved chemicals → nasal sensory cell → brain
chemicals → mucus membrane → sensory cells → brain
dissolved chemicals → sensory cells → olfactory nerve → brain
questions.explanation: Chemicals dissolve in the nasal mucus, stimulate the olfactory cells, and impulses pass along the olfactory nerve to the brain.

questions.stem: In mammals, the organ which performs digestive and endocrine functions is the
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces pancreatic juice and the hormones insulin and glucagon.

questions.stem: The chitin in the exoskeleton of many arthropods is strengthened by
questions.explanation: In crustaceans and other arthropods the chitin is hardened by calcium salts.

questions.stem: The construction of dams may lead to an increase in the prevalence of
options: typhoid fever, measles and yellow fever
questions.explanation: Dams create still and flowing water for mosquitoes, snails and blackflies, the vectors of these diseases.

questions.stem: Floating microscopic heterotrophs are mostly grouped as
questions.explanation: Zooplankton are tiny floating animals (heterotrophs); phytoplankton are autotrophs.

questions.stem: Vaccination is carried out in order to
options: increase the activity of white blood cells
increase the number of red blood cells
questions.explanation: A vaccine stimulates the body to produce antibodies, giving immunity.

questions.stem: A soil consisting of alumina and iron oxide is known as
questions.explanation: Laterite is a leached tropical soil rich in aluminium and iron oxides.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The sign + is used to indicate an association where an organism gains, while 0 is used where an organism is unaffected. An association indicated as + 0 is known as
questions.explanation: In commensalism one partner benefits and the other is unaffected.

questions.stem: Which of the following characterizes the white mangrove?
questions.explanation: The white mangrove (Avicennia) has breathing roots (pneumatophores); the red mangrove has stilt/prop roots.

questions.stem: If the offspring of a cross between a brown mouse (bb) and a black mouse (BB) are allowed to interbreed, how many different genotypes would result?
questions.explanation: F1 are all Bb; Bb x Bb gives BB, Bb and bb: 3 genotypes.

questions.stem: The biological factor that is unique to each individual is the
questions.explanation: Each individual (except identical twins) has a unique DNA profile; eye colour and blood group are shared by many.

questions.stem: From an evolutionary standpoint, the older a fossil-bearing rock is, the more likely it is to contain
questions.explanation: Invertebrates evolved before vertebrates, so older rocks contain invertebrate fossils.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The very bright colours in some types of mushroom
options: are a warning that they may be poisonous
indicate that they are very tasty
attract potential transporters of their spores
perform the same function as bright colours in flowers
questions.explanation: Bright (warning/aposematic) colouration signals that the mushroom may be poisonous.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The least adaptive feature for arboreal life is the
questions.explanation: Limbs, claws and a long tail help climbing and balance; countershading has nothing to do with life in trees.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of Lamarck’s theories?
options: some variations are more favourable to existence in a given environment than others
all living organisms are constantly involved in a struggle for existence
the size of a given population remains fairly constant
new species originate through the inheritance of acquired traits
questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed inheritance of acquired characters; the others are Darwinian ideas.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The loud cry made by a brooding hen when a predator is around is meant to
options: attract cocks to come and fight the predator
advertise the boundaries of its territory to intruders
warn its chicks and other chickens of impending danger
questions.explanation: The alarm call warns the chicks and other birds of danger.

questions.stem: The most important environmental factor which epiphytes in the rain forest compete for is
questions.explanation: Epiphytes grow on tall trees to reach the light in the dense forest canopy.

questions.stem: Which of the following features are all associated with monocots?
options: Fibrous root system, branched network of veins and one seed leaf
Fibrous root system, two seed leaves and floral parts in threes
One seed leaf, petals in threes or groups of threes and parallel venation of leaves
One seed leaf, net-veined leaves and petals in three or multiples of three
questions.explanation: Monocots have one cotyledon, parallel-veined leaves and floral parts in threes.

questions.stem: The set of fins that controls steering, balancing and change of direction and pitch in fish is
questions.explanation: The paired pectoral and pelvic fins control steering, balance, braking and pitch.

questions.stem: Coelom is absent in the class of animals termed
questions.explanation: Coelenterates (e.g. Hydra) are diploblastic and have no coelom.

questions.stem: A characteristic of vertebrates that is unique to mammals is
questions.explanation: Only mammals have a scrotum; the other features occur in other vertebrate classes too.

questions.stem: The order in which organic evolution has progressed in plants is
options: thallophyta, schizophyta, bryophyta, pteridophyta and spermatophyta
schizophyta, thallophyta, bryophyta, pteridophyta and spermatophyta
pteridophyta, spermatophyta, thallophyta, schizophyta and bryophyta
bryophyta, pteridophyta, spermatophyta, thallophyta and schizophyta
questions.explanation: From simplest to most complex: Schizophyta (bacteria/blue-green algae), Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Spermatophyta.

questions.stem: In which part of the human body does the secretion of the growth hormone occur?
questions.explanation: Growth hormone is secreted by the pituitary gland at the base of the brain.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Peripheral arrangement of vascular tissues in dicots is a characteristic of the internal structure of the
questions.explanation: In the dicot stem the vascular bundles form a ring near the periphery; in the root they are central.

questions.stem: The scapula and the ischium are part of the
questions.explanation: The scapula (pectoral girdle) and ischium (pelvic girdle) both belong to the appendicular skeleton.

questions.stem: Bacteria in the large intestine of man are important in the
options: synthesis of vitamins K and B12
synthesis of vitamins A and D
questions.explanation: Colon bacteria synthesise vitamin K and some B vitamins such as B12.

questions.stem: Short-sightedness can be corrected by lenses which are
questions.explanation: A concave (diverging) lens moves the image back onto the retina in myopia.

questions.stem: The inner ear contains two main organs, namely, the
questions.explanation: The inner ear has the cochlea (hearing) and semi-circular canals (balance).

questions.stem: For growth to occur in organisms, the rate of
options: catabolism must exceed that of anabolism
anabolism must exceed that of catabolism
questions.explanation: Growth requires building up (anabolism) to exceed breaking down (catabolism).

questions.stem: The production of violet colouration, when dilute NaOH solution is added to a solution of a food substance, followed by drops of 1% CuSO4 solution while shaking, indicates the presence of
questions.explanation: This is the Biuret test; a violet colour shows protein.

questions.stem: The greatest amount of energy will be obtained by the oxidation of 100 kg of
questions.explanation: Fat (butter) yields about twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrate or protein.

questions.stem: The chamber of the mammalian heart with the thickest wall is the
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood round the whole body, so it has the thickest wall.

questions.stem: Serum differs from blood plasma because it
options: contains soluble food and mineral salts
questions.explanation: Serum is plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed by clotting.

questions.stem: In an experiment to estimate the volume of air in a soil sample using a measuring cylinder, it was found that: initial volume of water = p cm3; volume of soil before mixing with water = q cm3; final volume of water after adding soil = r cm3. From the data above, which of the following deductions is correct?
questions.explanation: Water fills the air spaces in the soil, so the final volume is less than p + q; the difference is the air volume.

questions.stem: An ecological succession often leads to
questions.explanation: As succession proceeds toward climax, the number of species increases.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Atmospheric nitrogen is converted to soil nitrogen for plant use by
questions.explanation: Lightning fixes atmospheric nitrogen as oxides that form nitrates in the soil; nitrification makes nitrates available to plants. Of the options, this is the best.

questions.stem: I High birth rate and high immigration rate. II Low birth rate and high immigration rate. III Low mortality rate and low emigration rate. IV High mortality rate and high emigration rate. Which combination of the above can cause rapid overcrowding in climax biotic communities and human settlements?
questions.explanation: Many individuals added (high birth and immigration) and few lost (low mortality and emigration) cause overcrowding.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following are adaptations of animals to aquatic habitats?
options: Gills, streamlined bodies and lateral line
Lateral line, streamlined bodies and lungs
questions.explanation: Fish breathe with gills, swim with streamlined bodies and sense vibrations with the lateral line.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an adaptation of forest species?
questions.explanation: Tall rain-forest trees have buttress roots for support in shallow soils.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In a food chain, each succeeding level in a forward direction represents
options: an increase in the number of individuals
a decrease in the number of individuals
an increase in the biomass of individuals
a gain in the total energy being transferred
questions.explanation: Fewer individuals can be supported at each higher trophic level.

questions.stem: The disaster that would have the least destructive impact on animal life and balance in nature is
questions.explanation: Grasshopper pests mainly damage crops, while pollution, fires and oil spills destroy many forms of life.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The legs and beak of an egret resemble those of the heron because they
questions.explanation: Organisms occupying similar niches develop similar structural adaptations (long legs for wading and pointed beaks).

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: The factors that determine the distribution of vegetation zones are
questions.explanation: Climatic factors, mainly rainfall, temperature, light and humidity, determine vegetation zones.

questions.stem: A cross between an albino female and a genetically normal male will result in offspring that are
questions.explanation: aa x AA gives all Aa: phenotypically normal carriers.

questions.stem: The pollutants that contribute to the depletion of the ozone layer in the atmosphere are
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine which destroys ozone in the stratosphere.

questions.stem: Blood grouping in human beings is derived from combination of
questions.explanation: The ABO system is controlled by three alleles: IA, IB and i.

questions.stem: The older fossil-bearing rocks, in contrast to the more recent ones, are more likely to contain
questions.explanation: Invertebrates appeared long before birds, so older rocks are more likely to contain them.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: In a group of male Agama lizards, the one with the brightest head colour is the
questions.explanation: The dominant male displays the brightest colour to hold territory and attract females.

questions.stem: Examples of water-borne and sex-linked disease are
questions.explanation: Dracunculiasis (guinea worm) is water-borne and haemophilia is sex-linked.

questions.stem: The mutation theory of organic evolution was propounded by
questions.explanation: Hugo de Vries proposed that new species arise by sudden mutations.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A certain savanna grasshopper changes colour from green during the rainy season to brown during the dry season bush fires. The reason for these colour changes is that the
questions.explanation: Matching the green or burnt-brown background camouflages it from predators.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Complex social behaviour and organization are found mostly in
questions.explanation: Social insects (termites, bees, ants) show the most complex social organisation with castes.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following structural features are adapted for uses other than water conservation?
questions.explanation: Feathers serve flight and insulation; the others reduce water loss or store water.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: An association between the root nodule of a leguminous plant and Rhizobium sp. is known as
questions.explanation: Both benefit: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen for the legume and receives food and shelter (mutualism/symbiosis).

questions.stem: Amphibians are normally found
options: on dry land and in water
in water and on moist land
questions.explanation: Amphibians live in water and on moist land because their skin must stay moist.

questions.stem: Viviparity occurs mainly in the
questions.explanation: Most mammals give birth to live young (viviparity).

questions.stem: The jointed structure in insects that bears organs which are sensitive to touch, smell and vibration is the
questions.explanation: The jointed antennae carry sense organs for touch, smell and vibration.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups is the most advanced?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are seed plants, more advanced than ferns, mosses and thallophytes.

questions.stem: Most monocots are easily recognized by their
questions.explanation: Monocot leaves are typically long, narrow and sword-like with parallel veins.

questions.stem: Water fleas, wood lice and barnacles belong to the group
questions.explanation: Water fleas (Daphnia), woodlice and barnacles are crustaceans.

questions.stem: The mode of feeding in Amoeba and Hydra is
questions.explanation: Both ingest ready-made food (holozoic heterotrophs).

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms does not exist as a single free-living cell?
questions.explanation: Volvox is a colonial organism made of many cells.

questions.stem: The centre for learning and memory in the human brain is the
questions.explanation: The cerebrum controls intelligence, learning and memory.

questions.stem: Urea formation occurs in the
questions.explanation: Urea is formed in the liver (ornithine cycle) and excreted by the kidney.

questions.stem: The gas produced during tissue respiration can be identified by using
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide turns calcium hydroxide solution (lime water) milky.

questions.stem: A seedling grown in the dark is likely to be
questions.explanation: Seedlings grown in darkness are etiolated: pale, thin and elongated.

questions.stem: The enzyme invertase will hydrolyze sucrose to give
questions.explanation: Invertase (sucrase) splits sucrose into glucose and fructose.

questions.stem: When yeast respires anaerobically, it converts simple sugar to carbon (IV) oxide and
questions.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation: glucose gives ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: The transportation of oxygen and carbon (IV) oxide in mammals is carried out by
questions.explanation: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) carry oxygen and some carbon dioxide.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: The veins of the leaf are formed by the

questions.stem: When specimen X is mixed with a few drops of iodine solution, the appearance of a blue-black colour confirms that X is
questions.explanation: Iodine gives a blue-black colour with starch.

The factor that least affects food shortages in sub-Saharan Africa is
questions.explanation: Flooding, pests and drought destroy crops; mixed cropping is a farming practice that does not cause shortage.

questions.stem: The epiphytic habitat can best be described as
questions.explanation: Epiphytes live on trees, an arboreal habitat.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The highest percentage of energy in an ecosystem occurs at the level of the

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
