questions.stem: The distribution of plants in a rain forest is governed mainly by
questions.explanation: Light decreases from canopy to forest floor, determining the stratification of plants.

questions.stem: The probability of a baby being a boy or a girl depends on the condition of the
questions.explanation: All eggs carry X; the sperm carries X or Y and so determines the sex.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of blood groups and blood transfusion?
options: Group O is the universal recipient
Group A can donate to group A only
Group AB is the universal recipient
Group B can donate to group B only
questions.explanation: AB has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it can receive all groups.

questions.stem: In man, the ability to roll the tongue is a variation classified as
questions.explanation: Tongue rolling is a physiological (functional) variation.

questions.stem: Darwin is considered the first scientist who correctly explained the theory of
questions.explanation: Darwin explained organic evolution by natural selection.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The stem of a typical aquatic plant usually has many
questions.explanation: Aquatic stems have aerenchyma with large air cavities for buoyancy and aeration.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The role of the male adult honey bee is to
questions.explanation: Drones (males) only mate with the queen; workers do the other tasks.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The ability of an organism to live successfully in an environment is known as
questions.explanation: Adaptation is the possession of features that fit an organism to its environment.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The most important adaptation of xerophytes is the ability of the protoplasm to
options: resist being damaged by loss of water
store sugar and minerals in the vacuoles
questions.explanation: Xerophyte protoplasm tolerates desiccation without damage.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A green snake in green grass is able to escape notice from predators because of its
questions.explanation: Cryptic colouration matches the background so the animal blends in.

questions.stem: For heterotrophic organisms, competition is least caused by the inadequacy of
questions.explanation: Heterotrophs do not need light for food, so they rarely compete for it.

questions.stem: An Amoeba and an unlaid chicken egg are
questions.explanation: Each is a single cell; the unlaid egg is a single cell but not an organism.

questions.stem: In corms, food is usually stored in the
questions.explanation: A corm is a short swollen underground stem that stores food.

questions.stem: The organisms that move by means of flagella include
questions.explanation: Chlamydomonas and Euglena swim with flagella; Amoeba uses pseudopodia and Paramecium cilia.

questions.stem: The structures found only in plant cells are
questions.explanation: Cell walls and chloroplasts occur in plant cells but not animal cells.

questions.stem: A flower that has both stamens and pistil is said to be
questions.explanation: A perfect (bisexual) flower has both male and female parts.

questions.stem: When oil is poured into the breeding site of mosquitoes, it
questions.explanation: The oil film blocks the breathing tubes of the larvae and pupae at the water surface, suffocating them.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: One of the adaptations to life on trees by a monkey is its possession of digits which are
questions.explanation: Opposable digits allow the monkey to grip branches.

questions.stem: The community of plants in which the same species occur from year to year is the
questions.explanation: A climax community is stable and its species composition remains the same over the years.

questions.stem: The most common means of transmitting Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is
questions.explanation: Most HIV infections are acquired through unprotected sexual intercourse.

questions.stem: Plants tend to prevent overcrowding by means of efficient
questions.explanation: Dispersal carries seeds away from the parent plant, reducing overcrowding and competition.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: The physical and climatic factors of a region primarily determine the
options: kinds of animals inhabiting the area
types of plants found in the area
nature of the soil in the region
community of organisms in the region
questions.explanation: Climate (rainfall, temperature) mainly determines the vegetation; animals depend on the plants.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: A step in the movement of energy through an ecosystem is a description that best fits the term
questions.explanation: Each feeding step along which energy passes is a trophic level.

questions.stem: In a field experiment the frequency of waterleaf was observed to be 48 after 20 tosses of a 2 m2 quadrat. What is the density of the plant in the field?
questions.explanation: Area sampled = 20 x 2 = 40 m2; density = 48/40 = 1.2 per m2.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The supporting tissue of xylem is most poorly developed in
questions.explanation: Submerged plants are supported by water, so they have little xylem/supporting tissue.

questions.stem: The addition of lime to clay soil serves to
questions.explanation: Lime flocculates clay particles into crumbs, improving drainage and preventing water-logging.

questions.stem: The excessive use of agro-chemicals could lead to the pollution of
questions.explanation: Fertilizers and pesticides wash into rivers and lakes, causing eutrophication and poisoning.

questions.stem: In a population study using the transect method, a student is likely to record the highest number of species in
questions.explanation: The tropical rain forest has the greatest species diversity.

questions.stem: In his theory of evolution, Darwin implied that
options: the struggle for existence among living organisms is sporadic
the most successful organisms are those that best adapt to their environment
organs of the body which are not regularly used by an organism will disappear
any traits acquired by an organism during its lifetime can be passed on to its offspring
questions.explanation: Darwin’s natural selection: the best adapted survive; C and D are Lamarck’s ideas.

questions.stem: The carnassial teeth of a carnivorous animal consist of the
options: last upper premolar and the first lower molar
last upper molar and the last lower molar
first upper premolar and the first lower molar
first upper molar and the first lower molar
questions.explanation: In carnivores the carnassials are the last upper premolar and first lower molar, which shear flesh.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A feature of the caste systems of bees and termites is that
options: the kings are bigger than the queens
nuptial flight is performed by all members
questions.explanation: In both, workers are sterile individuals.

questions.stem: The structure that is common in the embryos of mammals, amphibians, birds, fishes and reptiles and which is an evidence of their common ancestry is the
questions.explanation: All vertebrate embryos develop gill slits (pharyngeal pouches), suggesting common ancestry.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Birds which are large with long straight pointed beaks, long necks and long legs are likely to be
questions.explanation: Wading fish-eaters (herons, egrets) have long legs, necks and pointed beaks.

questions.stem: Examples of organisms in which extracellular digestion occurs are
questions.explanation: Rhizopus secretes enzymes onto food, the housefly pours saliva on food, and Hydra begins digestion in its enteron.

questions.stem: The mammalian erythrocytes differ from other erythrocytes in that they are
questions.explanation: Mature mammalian red cells are biconcave discs without nuclei.

questions.stem: The presence of endoskeleton is characteristic of
questions.explanation: Vertebrates have an internal skeleton of bone or cartilage.

questions.stem: The capture and digestion of insects by a pitcher plant is a special form of nutrition termed
questions.explanation: Feeding on insects is a form of heterotrophic (holozoic) nutrition in an otherwise green plant.

questions.stem: When a marine fish was taken from the ocean and put in a tank of fresh water, it died after a short period because
options: the tank was too small compared to the large ocean
the body cells of the fish swelled and burst as a result of the hypotonic fresh water
the body cells of the fish shrank as their sap was hypertonic to the fresh water
there was no food in the tank, so the fish starved
questions.explanation: Fresh water is hypotonic, so water enters the cells by osmosis until they swell and burst.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of organs is located in the anterior half of the mammalian body cavity?
questions.explanation: The lungs and heart lie in the thoracic cavity at the front of the body cavity.

questions.stem: The mode of nutrition exhibited by a tapeworm is

questions.stem: A person that is obese must avoid meals containing

questions.stem: Tissue respiration is important for the

release of carbon (IV) oxide into the lungs
release of energy for body use
exhalation of carbon (IV) oxide from lungs

questions.stem: To select and retain the desirable trait of large body size which a farmer has observed in his herd, the farmer needs to
options: feed the animals in the herd with more food
cross-breed his animals with a different herd
inbreed the animals in his herd
questions.explanation: Inbreeding (selective mating within the herd) fixes and retains the desired trait; cross-breeding introduces other traits.

questions.stem: In a population of living things, the parameters of size, height, weight and colour are examples of

questions.stem: The umbrella-shaped fruiting body of a fully developed mushroom is the

questions.stem: The similarity among organisms belonging to the same group will be least within each

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals

questions.stem: Organisms I, II, III and IV have surface/volume ratios of 1:2, 1:3, 1:4 and 1:5 respectively. The organism that is likely to have the most complex transport system is

questions.stem: The part of the mammalian digestive system where absorption of nutrients takes place is the
questions.explanation: Digested food is absorbed through the villi of the ileum.

questions.stem: The dark reaction of photosynthesis involves the
options: release of oxygen and the splitting of water
photolysis of water and the production of starch
reduction of carbon (IV) oxide to organic compounds
splitting of water into hydrogen ions
questions.explanation: In the dark (light-independent) stage CO2 is reduced to carbohydrate; photolysis occurs in the light stage.

questions.stem: The most important hormone that induces the ripening of fruit is
questions.explanation: Ethylene is the fruit-ripening hormone.

questions.stem: Metabolic production of urea is carried out in the
questions.explanation: Urea is made in the liver by deamination of excess amino acids.

questions.stem: In mammalian males, the excretory and reproductive systems share the
questions.explanation: The urethra carries both urine and semen.

questions.stem: The best method of propagating sugarcane is by
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is propagated vegetatively by stem cuttings (setts).

questions.stem: The response of plants to external stimuli in a non-directional manner is known as
questions.explanation: Nastic movements are non-directional responses (e.g. folding of Mimosa leaves).

questions.stem: Homologous pairs of chromosomes separate during
questions.explanation: Homologous chromosomes pair and separate in the first division of meiosis.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms

questions.explanation: Acidic emissions (e.g. SO2) change the soil and water pH, limiting plant growth.

questions.stem: The pioneer organisms in ecological succession are usually the
questions.explanation: Lichens are the first colonisers of bare rock.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Mycorrhiza is an association between fungi and
questions.explanation: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association of fungi with the roots of higher plants.

questions.stem: A density-dependent factor that regulates the population size of organisms is
questions.explanation: Disease spreads faster in crowded populations, so its effect depends on density.

questions.stem: The most effective method of dealing with non-biodegradable pollution is by
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable waste does not rot, so recycling is the best method.

questions.stem: The correct sequence of biomes from northern to southern Nigeria is
options: estuarine → tropical rain forest → guinea savanna → sahel savanna
sahel savanna → sudan savanna → guinea savanna → tropical rainforest → estuarine
sahel savanna → tropical rain forest → estuarine → guinea savanna
guinea savanna → sudan savanna → tropical rainforest → sahel savanna → estuarine
questions.explanation: From north to south: Sahel, Sudan, Guinea savanna, rain forest and then the coastal estuarine swamps.

questions.stem: One example of fossil fuels is
questions.explanation: Coal is formed from fossilised plant remains.

questions.stem: An organism that has been extensively used to test the chromosome theory of heredity is
questions.explanation: T. H. Morgan used the fruit fly Drosophila to establish the chromosome theory.

questions.stem: A feature associated with the Y-chromosome in humans is
questions.explanation: Facial hair is a male (XY) characteristic.

questions.stem: The type of reproduction that leads to variation in animal and plant populations is
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents, producing variation.

questions.stem: If a DNA strand has a base sequence TCA, its complementary strand must be
questions.explanation: T pairs with A and C with G, so TCA pairs with AGT.

questions.stem: Which of the following requires the use of carbon dating to prove that evolution has occurred?
questions.explanation: The age of fossils is determined by carbon (radiometric) dating.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Spines and shells on animals are adaptations for
questions.explanation: Spines and shells protect animals physically from predators.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The inactive state exhibited by an animal during hot dry seasons is termed
questions.explanation: Aestivation is dormancy in the hot dry season; hibernation is in the cold season.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.explanation: Mandibulate mouthparts (e.g. cockroach, grasshopper) bite and chew solid food.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: An example of cryptic colouration is the
options: bright marks on a poisonous tropical frog on variegated leaves
bright colour of an insect-pollinated flower
mottled colours on moths that rest on lichens
questions.explanation: Mottled moths blend with the lichen background, hiding them from predators.

questions.stem: An argument against Lamarck’s theory of evolution is that
options: acquired traits cannot be passed on to the offspring
disuse of body part cannot weaken the part
disused part is dropped off in the offspring
traits cannot be acquired through constant use of body parts
questions.explanation: Characters acquired during life are not genetic and so are not inherited.

questions.stem: The opening of the stoma is controlled by the
options: decrease in solute concentration in the guard cells
increase in solute concentration in the guard cells
questions.explanation: Higher solute concentration in the guard cells draws in water; they become turgid and the pore opens.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals

questions.stem: The breakdown of fats and oils into simpler absorbable compounds is catalyzed by the group of enzymes called

questions.stem: The anaerobic fermentation of a glucose molecule yields

questions.stem: The type of reproduction that is common to both Hydra and yeast is
questions.explanation: Both Hydra and yeast reproduce asexually by budding.

questions.stem: Epigeal germination of a seed is characterized by
options: lack of growth of the hypocotyl
more rapid elongation of the hypocotyl than the epicotyl
more rapid elongation of the epicotyl than the hypocotyl
equal growth rate of both the hypocotyl and epicotyl
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination the hypocotyl elongates faster and carries the cotyledons above ground.

questions.stem: All living cells require water because it
options: is a medium that neutralizes acids in cells
is the main source of energy for the cells
prevents the development of diseases in cells
is a medium for all metabolic reactions
questions.explanation: Metabolic reactions take place in aqueous solution.

questions.stem: The surface of an alveolus in a mammal is well supplied with tiny blood vessels known as
questions.explanation: A dense capillary network surrounds each alveolus for gaseous exchange.

questions.stem: Nervous control differs from hormonal control in that the former
questions.explanation: Nervous responses are rapid and short-lived; hormonal effects are slower and longer-lasting.

questions.stem: Identical twins inherit their genes from
questions.explanation: Identical twins come from one zygote (one egg fertilised by one sperm) that splits.

questions.stem: Paternity disputes can most accurately be resolved through the use of
questions.explanation: DNA profiling compares the child’s DNA directly with the alleged father’s; blood groups can only exclude.

questions.stem: In a Mendelian cross of red and white varieties of the four o’clock plant, the F1 generation expresses incomplete dominance by having flowers which are
questions.explanation: With incomplete dominance the heterozygote (RW) is intermediate: pink.

questions.stem: The absence of special food and water-conducting systems restricts the body size in
questions.explanation: Algae and bryophytes lack vascular tissue; ferns (pteridophytes) have it.

questions.stem: A peculiar characteristic of mammals is that they
questions.explanation: Skin glands such as sebaceous glands are found only in mammals; birds are also warm-blooded.

questions.stem: The rods in the retina of the eye are examples of
questions.explanation: Rods are individual light-sensitive cells.

questions.stem: The larval stage of a mosquito is called
questions.explanation: Mosquito larvae are called wrigglers from their movement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of intraspecific competition?
options: Yam and potato shoots growing out through the same window
A lizard and an ant-eater chasing an insect
A worker termite and a soldier in a limited space
A hawk and an eagle targeting the same chicken
questions.explanation: Worker and soldier termites are members of the same species; the others involve different species.

questions.stem: Rodents gnaw on food with their

options: storing water in large parenchyma cells

questions.stem: A caterpillar and an aphid living in different parts of the same plant can be said to
questions.explanation: They share a habitat but feed differently in different places, so their niches differ.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The progressive loss of energy at each level in a food chain leads to
options: a decrease in biomass at each successive level
an increase in the number of organisms at each successive level
an increase in the total weight of living matter at each successive level
an increase in biomass at each successive level
questions.explanation: Less energy is available at each level, so less biomass can be supported.

questions.stem: The soil type that will be most difficult to plough in a wet season is one that is

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.stem: The scarcity of food causes a sudden decrease in population size by
questions.explanation: Starvation increases deaths, rapidly reducing population size.

questions.stem: A state in Nigeria that is most susceptible to desert encroachment is
questions.explanation: Katsina lies in the far north on the edge of the Sahel.

questions.stem: A farm practice that results in the loss of soil fertility is
questions.explanation: Continuous cropping exhausts soil nutrients without time for recovery.

questions.stem: Which of the following characterizes a mature plant cell?
options: the cytoplasm fills up the entire cell space
the nucleus is pushed to the centre of the cell
the cell wall is made up of cellulose
the nucleus is small and irregular in shape
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose; in a mature plant cell a large vacuole pushes the cytoplasm and nucleus to the periphery.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the nucleus of a cell?
options: it controls the life processes of the cell
it translates genetic information for the manufacture of proteins
it stores and carries hereditary information
it is reservoir of energy for the cell
questions.explanation: Energy is released in the mitochondria, not stored in the nucleus; the nucleus controls the cell and carries hereditary information.

questions.stem: The dominant phase in the life cycle of a fern is the?
questions.explanation: The fern plant itself (fronds, rhizome, roots) is the diploid sporophyte; the prothallus is the small gametophyte.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.explanation: Birds incubate their eggs and feed and protect their young; the others abandon their eggs.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups of cells is devoid of true nuclei
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is B because Monera (bacteria and blue-green algae) are prokaryotic cells without a true nucleus; viruses are not cells at all.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the transverse section of a dicot stem?
options: the epidermis is completely encircled by the cortex
the xylem is more interiorly located than the phloem
the cambium lies between the cortex and the vascular bundles
the vascular bundles are randomly scattered within the cortex
questions.explanation: In a dicot stem vascular bundle the xylem lies towards the centre and the phloem towards the outside, with cambium between them.

questions.stem: The mode of nutrition of sun dew and bladder wort can be described as

questions.stem: The primary structure responsible for pumping blood for circulation through the mammalian circulatory systems is the

questions.stem: Circulation of blood to all parts of the body except the lungs is through

questions.stem: Yeast respires anaerobically to convert simple sugar to carbon (IV) oxide and

questions.stem: The sheet of muscle that separates the thoracic and the abdominal cavities is the

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals

questions.stem: In the male reproductive system of a mammal, sperm is stored in the

questions.stem: Chemosynthetic organisms are capable of manufacturing their food from simple inorganic substances through the process of

questions.stem: The part of the human gut that has an acidic content is the
questions.explanation: Gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid into the stomach.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem:
I. Stomata -> Spirogyra

III. Malpighian tubule -> Mammal
IV. Contractile vacuole -> Protozoa.

questions.explanation: Contractile vacuoles occur in protozoa; Spirogyra has no stomata, earthworms breathe through the skin and Malpighian tubules are in insects.

questions.stem: A food chain always begins with a
questions.explanation: Every food chain starts with a producer (green plant) that traps solar energy.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Mycorrhizae promote plant growth by
options: absorbing inorganic ions from the soil
helping it to utilize atmospheric nitrogen
questions.explanation: The fungal partner in a mycorrhiza increases the absorption of mineral ions (e.g. phosphate) from the soil for the plant.

questions.stem: The barrier between maternal and foetal blood is the

questions.stem: The blood component that has the greatest affinity for oxygen is the
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes contain haemoglobin, which combines readily with oxygen.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms is mainly found in the marine habitat?
questions.explanation: The dogfish is a marine cartilaginous fish; Achatina is a land snail and Tilapia a freshwater fish.

questions.stem: The two halves of the pelvic girdle are joined together at the
questions.explanation: The two innominate bones meet ventrally at the pubic symphysis.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem:
I. Adoption of appropriate nocturnal habits
II. Burrowing
III. Adjusting their internal body temperature.
IV. Possession of many sweat pores.
Which of the above are ways in which desert animals adapt to extreme heat of the environment?
questions.explanation: Desert animals avoid daytime heat by being nocturnal and burrowing; many sweat pores would waste scarce water.

questions.stem: Low annual rainfall, sparse vegetation, high diurnal temperatures and cold nights are characteristic features of the
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is B because very low rainfall, sparse vegetation, hot days and cold nights describe a desert, not the Guinea savanna.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: The activity of an organism which affects the survival of another organism in the same habitat constitutes
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is C because effects of living organisms on one another are biotic factors; edaphic factors are soil factors.

questions.stem: The average number of individuals of a species per unit area of the habitat is the
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is A because number of individuals per unit area is population density; population size is the total number.

questions.stem: The vector for yellow fever is
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is A because the yellow fever virus is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito; Anopheles transmits malaria.

questions.stem: The loss of soil through erosion can be reduced by
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is B because crop rotation (with cover crops) keeps the soil covered and its structure intact, reducing erosion; watering and irrigation can increase it.

questions.stem: The protozoan plasmodium falciparum is transmitted by

questions.stem: A dilute solution of phenylthiocarbamide tastes bitter to some people and is tasteless to others. This is an example of

questions.stem: Thyroxine and adrenalin are examples of hormones which control
questions.explanation: Hormones such as thyroxine and adrenaline influence behaviour (activity, alertness, aggression), a physiological/behavioural variation.

questions.stem: A pair of genes that control a trait is referred to as
questions.explanation: Alternative forms of a gene occupying the same locus and controlling one trait are alleles.

questions.stem: The chromosome number of a cell before and after the process of meiosis is conventionally represented as
questions.explanation: Meiosis is reduction division: a diploid (2n) cell gives haploid (n) cells.

questions.explanation: Aa x Aa gives AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1, so homozygous recessive aa = 1/4.

questions.stem: At what stage in the life history of a mammal is the sex of an individual set?
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because sex is determined at fertilisation (conception) by whether the sperm carries an X or a Y chromosome.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The main distinguishing features between the soldier termite and other members of the caste are the
options: presence of wings, possession of a small head and large thorax
presence of wings, possession of a large thorax and a small head
absence of wings, possession of strong mandibles and a large head
absence of wings, possession of big head and the absence of mandible
questions.explanation: Soldier termites are wingless with a large, hard head bearing strong mandibles for defence.

questions.stem: The flippers of a whale and the fins of a fish are examples of
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because whale flippers and fish fins are analogous structures that evolved separately for swimming, an example of convergent evolution.

questions.stem: In which of the following species is the biomass of an individual the smallest?
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is C because a single Spirogyra filament (a microscopic alga) has far less mass than an individual lizard, toad or fish.

questions.stem: Seed plants are divided into
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because seed plants (spermatophytes) are divided into gymnosperms (naked seeds) and angiosperms (enclosed seeds); monocots and dicots are subdivisions of angiosperms.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: In which of the following groups of vertebrates is parental care mostly exhibited?
questions.explanation: Mammals show the highest degree of parental care: internal development, suckling and prolonged protection of the young.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The adaptive importance of nuptial flight from termite colonies is to
options: disperse the reproductives in order to establish new colonies
provide abundant food for birds and other animals during the early rains
ensure cross-breeding between members of one colony and another
expel the reproductives so as to provide enough food for other members
questions.explanation: The swarming winged reproductives disperse, pair and found new colonies.

questions.stem: Which of the following can cause shrinkage of living cells?
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution cells lose water by osmosis and shrink (plasmolysis/crenation).

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of leucocytes?
options: they are most numerous and ramify all cells
they are involved in blood clotting
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is C because white blood cells are relatively large and possess nuclei; they are fewer than red cells and clotting is due to platelets.

questions.stem: The conversion of a nutrient into a molecule in the body of a consumer is referred to as

questions.stem: The ability of living organism to detect and respond to changes in the environment is referred to as

questions.stem: In mammals, the exchange of nutrients and metabolic products occurs in the

questions.stem: An example of an endospermous seed is

the transport of gases and water
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and mineral salts; phloem conducts manufactured food.

questions.stem: Which of the following organs regulates the levels of water, salts, hydrogen ions and urea in the mammalian blood?
questions.explanation: The kidney performs osmoregulation and excretion, controlling water, salts, pH and urea.

questions.stem: The sequence of the one-way gaseous exchange mechanism in a fish is

questions.stem: The type of asexual reproduction that is common to both Paramecium and protists is

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In nature, plants and animals are perpetually engaged in mutualism because

they utilize respiratory wastes of each other

questions.stem: The interaction of a community of organisms with its abiotic environment constitutes

questions.stem: Habitats are generally classified into

questions.stem: Which of the following groups of environmental factors are density- dependent?
options: Food, salinity, accumulation of metabolites and light
Food predation, disease and accumulation of metabolites
questions.explanation: Food supply, predation, disease and accumulation of wastes intensify as population density rises; temperature, salinity and light do not depend on density.

questions.stem: Millet, sorghum, maize and onions are common crops growth in Nigeria in the

questions.stem: In which of the following biomes is the south western part of Nigeria located?

questions.stem: The inheritable characters that are determined by a gene located on the X- chromosome is

traits are acquired through the use of body parts

questions.stem: Which of the following is most advanced in the evolutionary trend of animals?

questions.stem: Which of the following is the lowest category of classification?

questions.stem: Plants that show secondary growth are usually found among the

questions.stem: The fungi are distinct group of eukaryotes mainly because they have

questions.stem: An arthropod that is destructive at early stage of its life cycle is

questions.stem: An animal body that can be cut along its axis in any plane to give two identical parts is said to be

questions.stem: Which of the following possesses mammary gland?
questions.explanation: The whale is a mammal and suckles its young; the others are fishes.

questions.stem: The feature that links birds to reptiles in evolution is the possession of

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals

questions.explanation: Roots absorb water through their surface and root hairs, so they lack a waterproof cuticle.

questions.stem: In the mammalian male reproductive system, the part that serves as a passage for both urine and semen is the

questions.stem: In plants which of the following is required in minute quantities for growth?

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms is both parasitic and autotrophic?

questions.stem: A function of the hydrochloric acid produced in the human stomach during digestion is to

break up food into smaller particles
questions.explanation: The acid medium stops salivary amylase (ptyalin) and provides the acid pH for pepsin; it also kills germs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a polysaccharide?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a polymer of glucose (polysaccharide); sucrose and maltose are disaccharides and glucose a monosaccharide.

questions.stem: In the kidney of mammals, the site of ultrafiltration is the

questions.stem: Which of the following is involved in secondary thickening in plants?
questions.explanation: Secondary thickening involves the vascular cambium (new xylem and phloem) and the cork cambium (bark).

questions.stem: An example of a fruit that develops from a single carpel is

questions.stem: The autonomic nervous system consists of neurons that control the

questions.stem: Plants of temperate origin can be grown in tropical areas in the vegetation zones of the

questions.stem: The water cycle is maintained mainly by
options: evaporation of water in the environment
evaporation and condensation of water in the environment
condensation of water in the environment
questions.explanation: Water evaporates, condenses into clouds and returns as rain, so evaporation and condensation drive the cycle.

questions.stem: Organisms living in an estuarine habitat are adapted to
options: survive only in water with low salinity
feed only on phytoplankton and dead organic matter
questions.explanation: Estuaries mix fresh and sea water with the tides, so salinity changes widely.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.stem: The most likely first colonizers of a bare rock are

questions.stem: The carrying capacity of a habitat is reached when the population growth begins to

questions.stem: The abiotic factors that control human population include
questions.explanation: Flooding and earthquakes are non-living (abiotic) factors; disease and famine are biotic.

questions.stem: An indigenous method of renewing and maintaining soil fertility is by

questions.stem: The diseases caused by water-borne pathogens include
questions.explanation: Typhoid and cholera are spread through contaminated water.

persons of blood groups A and B can donate or receive blood from each other

A person of blood group O can donate only to a person of blood group O

questions.stem: The correct base pairing for DNA is

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The basking of Agama lizards in the sun is to

raise their body temperature to become active
questions.explanation: Lizards are cold-blooded and bask to warm their bodies to an active temperature.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The significance of a very large number of termites involved in nuptial swarming is to
options: provide birds with plenty of food
ensure their perpetuation despite predatory pressure
search for a favourable place to breed
ensure that every individual gets a mate
questions.explanation: Many swarmers are eaten, so large numbers ensure some survive to found new colonies.

questions.stem: The use and disuse of body parts and the inheritance of acquired traits were used to explain

the organism has a pair of jointed appendages
the body is not divided into a number of segments
the body is covered by chitin

Both are active during the day
the abdomen of moth is fatter than that of butterfly
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because option A is reversed (butterflies fold their wings vertically over the back at rest, moths hold them flat); moths have a stouter abdomen.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of feathers is used for flight in birds?

questions.explanation: Birds of prey grip prey with sharp claws (talons) and tear flesh with a hooked beak.

questions.stem: The lowest level of organization in living organisms is

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most complex according to their cellular level of organization?

II. Growth is specific with definite shape

questions.explanation: Light penetration falls rapidly with depth, limiting photosynthesis and hence productivity.

questions.stem: Which of the following group of organisms feeds directly on green plants?
questions.explanation: Primary consumers (herbivores) feed directly on producers.

questions.stem: A characteristic feature of tropical rainforest is that it
options: Contains large number of plant species
Contains fewer number of plant species
Has total annual rainfall of less than 50cm
questions.explanation: Tropical rainforests have very high species diversity and heavy rainfall.

questions.stem: The study of how and why population size change over time is

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of small pox?

It can effectively be controlled by vaccination

questions.stem: A biotic factor which affects the distribution and abundance of organisms in a terrestrial habitat is
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because competition is a living (biotic) factor, while pH, temperature and light are abiotic.

questions.stem: The eye defect that arises because the cornea is not curved smoothly is
questions.explanation: Uneven curvature of the cornea causes astigmatism.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of parasitism?
options: a squirrel living in an abandoned nest of a bird
mistletoe growing on an orange tree
fungi growing on a dead tree branch
cattle egrets taking ticks from the body of cattle
questions.explanation: Mistletoe draws water and salts from its host orange tree.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors can bring about competition in a population?
questions.explanation: Drought makes water and food scarce, so members compete for them.

questions.stem: Stunted growth and poor root development are a result of a deficiency in
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is needed for root development and growth.

questions.stem: The cell organelle solely responsible for respiration is the
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle and electron transport) takes place in the mitochondrion.

questions.stem: Which of the following will be true of a dog (dog II) which lost its tail in an accident if it mates with another dog (dog III)?
options: all its offspring will be born without tails
3/4 of its offspring will be born without tails
none of its offspring will be born without a tail
1/4 of its offspring will be born without tails
questions.explanation: A tail lost by accident is an acquired character and is not inherited.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following structures is a protective adaptive feature of the Agama lizard to the environment?
questions.explanation: The dry scaly skin protects the lizard against desiccation and injury.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following adapts an insect for feeding?
questions.explanation: Mouthparts are modified for the insect's mode of feeding.

questions.stem: Which of the following results from the cross between Yy and Yy?
questions.explanation: Yy x Yy gives 1 YY : 2 Yy : 1 yy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the carbon cycle?
questions.explanation: Nitrate formation belongs to the nitrogen cycle.

questions.stem: I. Tissues  II. System  III. Cell  IV. Organs. Which of the above is the level of organization of a leaf?
questions.explanation: A leaf is made of several tissues working together, so it is an organ.

questions.stem: In cellular respiration, energy is stored in the form of
questions.explanation: Respiratory energy is stored in ATP.

questions.stem: The principal organ for the manufacture of food in autotrophy is the
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs mainly in the green leaf.

questions.stem: A disease that results from lack of iodine in the diet of humans is
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency causes goitre (enlarged thyroid).

questions.stem: The process whereby some organisms with certain favourable features get established in an area is
questions.explanation: Organisms with favourable variations survive and establish themselves by natural selection.

questions.stem: The rise and fall of ocean water during the day is referred to as
questions.explanation: The periodic rise and fall of sea level is the tide.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a producer in an aquatic habitat?
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is A because Nymphaea (water lily) is a green aquatic plant; Planaria is an animal and Dryopteris is a terrestrial fern.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The relationship that exists between a shark and Remora is
questions.explanation: The remora benefits from scraps and transport while the shark is unaffected: commensalism.

questions.stem: I. Tissue  II. System  III. Cell  IV. Organ. The correct sequence of increasing level of complexity is
questions.explanation: Cell, tissue, organ, system = III-I-IV-II.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an inheritable disease?
questions.explanation: Poliomyelitis is caused by a virus, not inherited.

questions.stem: Which of the fingerprint types occurs most frequently in the population of human beings?
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because loops are the commonest fingerprint pattern (about 60-65% of people), whorls next and arches rarest.

questions.stem: Beriberi results from a deficiency of
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is C because beriberi is caused by lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine).

questions.stem: Bacteria which add atmospheric nitrogen to the soil are
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert atmospheric N2 into nitrogen compounds in the soil.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: The spines of the hedgehog are an adaptive feature for
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because the hedgehog rolls into a ball with spines outward to protect itself from predators.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following instruments is used to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is A because a thermometer measures temperature (an anemometer measures wind speed).

questions.stem: In humans, puffiness and water retention in the body is a possible symptom of
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is C because failing kidneys cannot remove excess water and salts, causing oedema (puffiness).

questions.stem: The theory of evolution which postulates that all living organisms have a common ancestor was proposed by
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because Darwin's theory of descent with modification holds that all organisms share common ancestry.

questions.stem: Mammals require roughage in their food to
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is C because roughage adds bulk that helps peristalsis move food along the gut.

questions.stem: Variation can occur among offspring of living organisms because
options: zygotes are produced by cross fertilisation
they are produced by binary fission
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because cross fertilisation combines genes from two parents, producing variation; binary fission gives identical offspring.

questions.stem: The lowest unit of classification is the
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because species is the lowest unit; kingdom is the highest.

questions.stem: Two important processes involved in the absorption and transport of materials in plants are
questions.explanation: Water enters roots by osmosis and solutes move by diffusion.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: A series of organisms existing in an ecosystem through which energy is transferred can be referred to as
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is B because a single linear series of organisms through which energy passes is a food chain; a food web is interlinked chains.

questions.stem: In which part of Nigeria are Mangrove swamps found?
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is B because mangrove swamps fringe the brackish coastal Niger Delta.

questions.stem: In a small unicellular organism, diffusion is sufficient for transport because
options: the surface area to volume ratio is small
materials have to move over long distance
the surface area to volume ratio is large
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because small organisms have a large surface area to volume ratio and short diffusion distances.

questions.stem: The first vertebrates to venture out of water and live on land are the
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because amphibians were the first vertebrates to colonise land; reptiles came later.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following factors mostly determine the major biomes of the world?
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because climate (temperature and rainfall) determines the major biomes.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: I. Strong winds  II. High temperature  III. Dry and porous soils. Which group of plants are specially adapted to grow under the environmental conditions stated above?
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is C because xerophytes are adapted to dry, hot, windy conditions.

questions.stem: Severe diarrhoea, dehydration and weakness are symptoms of
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is A because cholera causes profuse watery diarrhoea and dehydration.

questions.stem: A common characteristic found among the crustaceans is the possession of
options: a pair of walking legs on each segment
four pairs of walking legs on the cephalothorax
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because crustaceans have two pairs of antennae (insects have one pair).

questions.stem: In which of the following groups of invertebrates are flagella and cilia found?
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is B because flagella and cilia are locomotory organelles of protists such as Euglena and Paramecium.

questions.stem: Physiological variation in human population is evident in the
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because tongue rolling is a physiological variation; fingerprints, appearance, height and weight are morphological.

questions.stem: In photosynthesis, oxygen is liberated during
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is B because oxygen comes from the light-driven splitting (photolysis) of water.

questions.stem: The piercing and sucking mouth parts are found in
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes pierce skin and suck blood; the others have biting and chewing mouthparts.

questions.stem: The hormones that regulate plant growth are
questions.explanation: Auxins and gibberellins promote cell elongation and growth.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of organisms exhibit parasitic association?
questions.explanation: The tsetse fly feeds on cattle blood and transmits trypanosomes.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following groups of animals can withstand the rigour of the arid land?
questions.explanation: Locusts, camels, lizards and snakes are adapted to dry habitats; earthworms, snails, ducks and lungfish need moisture.

questions.stem: Suture joint is found in the
questions.explanation: Sutures are immovable joints between the skull bones.

questions.stem: The organelle responsible for osmoregulation in Paramecium is
questions.explanation: The contractile vacuole expels excess water from Paramecium.

questions.stem: The platelets in mammalian blood are responsible for
questions.explanation: Platelets release thromboplastin, starting blood clotting.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: The most important factor that determines the different types of vegetation is
questions.explanation: Rainfall is the main factor separating forest, savanna and desert vegetation.

questions.stem: When testing for the presence of starch in a leaf, the reason for dipping the decolourised leaf in hot water is to
questions.explanation: Alcohol makes the leaf brittle; dipping it in hot water softens it before adding iodine.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The relationship between remora and shark can best be described as
questions.explanation: The remora benefits while the shark is neither harmed nor helped.

questions.stem: The major characteristic of a fresh water habitat is the possession of
questions.explanation: Fresh water has a very low salt content.

questions.stem: The causative organism of cholera is
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae.

questions.stem: The process that takes place in the dark stage of photosynthesis is
questions.explanation: In the dark (light-independent) stage CO2 is reduced to carbohydrate using hydrogen from the light stage.

questions.stem: Chlorofluorocarbons are air pollutants that originate from
questions.explanation: CFCs were used as refrigerants in cooling systems.

questions.stem: Which of the following is organ level of organisation?
questions.explanation: The onion bulb is an organ (a modified shoot); Paramecium is a cell, Volvox a colony and Hydra a tissue-level organism.

questions.stem: The simplest form of reproduction is
questions.explanation: Binary fission is the simple division of one cell into two.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of wind-pollinated flowers?
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers do not need to attract insects, so they lack nectar and scent.

questions.stem: The process required for formation of gametes in sexual reproduction is
questions.explanation: Gametes are haploid cells formed by meiosis.

questions.stem: In an experiment to determine the humus in a soil sample the following results were obtained: Mass of dish = 20 g; Mass of dry soil = 7.5 g; Mass of dish + soil after burning = 25 g. The percentage of humus in the given sample is
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because humus burnt off = (20 + 7.5) - 25 = 2.5 g, and 2.5/7.5 x 100 = 33.3%.

questions.stem: In a 15 m^2 habitat, the total number of Tridax counted using a 1.6 m^2 quadrat thrown randomly 50 times was 400. What is the density of Tridax (per m^2)?
questions.explanation: Mean per quadrat = 400/50 = 8; density = 8/1.6 = 5 per m^2.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sex-linked character?
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because colour blindness is carried on the X chromosome; albinism is autosomal.

questions.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
questions.stem: The outermost tissue of the herbaceous roots is the
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is C because the root is covered by the epidermis (piliferous layer); roots have no cuticle.

questions.stem: The respective tissues that transport water and manufactured food in plants are
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water; phloem carries manufactured food.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: An adaptive feature of plants in the savanna is
questions.explanation: Thick, fissured corky bark protects savanna trees from fire and water loss.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A grasshopper's cuticle becomes green during the season and black after fire. The reason for the change is to
questions.explanation: Matching the colour of the background camouflages the grasshopper from predators.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most advanced plant?
questions.explanation: Dryopteris (a fern) has vascular tissue, unlike the bryophyte Marchantia and the algae.

questions.stem: The soil type with the least ability to retain nutrients is
questions.explanation: Sand has large particles and pores, so nutrients are leached easily.

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: A humming bird is able to feed on nectar because its beak is
questions.explanation: A long slender beak reaches nectar deep inside flowers.

questions.stem: The effect of overcrowding is
questions.explanation: Overcrowding increases competition, driving individuals to emigrate.

questions.stem: The vertebrae that allow the skull to nod and rotate are
questions.explanation: The atlas allows nodding and the axis allows rotation of the head.

questions.stem: The component of the cell that determines paternity resides in the
questions.explanation: Nuclear DNA, used in paternity testing, is in the nucleus.

questions.stem: Morphological variation in humans includes
options: height, skin colour and tongue rolling
questions.explanation: Weight, fingerprints and body shape are all visible structural features; tongue rolling and blood group are physiological.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct about blood transfusion?
options: Group AB can only receive from groups A and B and not from group O
Group O can receive from groups A and B and from AB
Group B can only donate to blood group B and not to AB and O
Group O can donate to groups A, B and AB but cannot receive
questions.explanation: Group O is the universal donor but can receive only group O blood.

questions.stem: A group of closely related organisms capable of interbreeding to produce fertile offspring are known as members of a
questions.explanation: A species is a group of organisms that interbreed to give fertile offspring.

questions.stem: A beaker of pond water containing a few specimens of Euglena was placed in a dark room for two weeks. At the end of this period, the specimens of Euglena were still alive because they were
options: able to carry out holozoic nutrition
able to carry out photosynthesis using carbon dioxide in the pond water
better adapted to life in darkness than to life in light
questions.explanation: Without light Euglena switches to heterotrophic (holozoic/saprophytic) feeding.

questions.stem: The cytoplasm of the cell is considered a very important component because it
options: regulates the amount of energy in the cell
is the outermost part of the cell
is solely responsible for cell division
questions.explanation: The organelles are suspended in the cytoplasm, where many reactions occur.

questions.stem: Red blood cells were found to have burst open after being placed in distilled water for an hour. This phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation: Water enters red cells by osmosis until they burst: haemolysis.

questions.stem: The curvature movement of plants in response to the stimulus of water is called
questions.explanation: Growth curvature towards water is hydrotropism.

questions.stem: The longest bone in the body is the
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is not a skeletal material?
questions.explanation: Chitin, cartilage and bone are skeletal materials; muscle is not.

questions.stem: The reason why the flow of blood through the capillaries is very slow is
options: because the walls of capillaries are very thin
to ensure that the individual does not get dizzy
to allow adequate time for exchange of materials
questions.explanation: Slow flow allows time for exchange of materials with tissues.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups of organisms has kidney as their excretory organ?
questions.explanation: All vertebrates excrete with kidneys; annelids use nephridia, insects Malpighian tubules, tapeworms flame cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following features is not a characteristic of arteries? Arteries
options: possess valves at intervals throughout their length
have thick muscular and elastic walls
carry blood away from the heart
transport oxygenated blood with the exception of the pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: Valves along their length are a feature of veins, not arteries.

questions.stem: What physiological term can be used to describe the regulation of the body temperature of a lizard?
questions.explanation: A lizard's body temperature changes with the environment: it is poikilothermic.

questions.stem: The reason why hospitals use saline solutions as drip instead of water is
options: to prevent contamination of the body
to maintain the composition of body fluids
to increase the number of blood cells
questions.explanation: Saline is isotonic with body fluids, so cells neither swell nor shrink.

questions.stem: The part of the ear which contains nerve cells sensitive to sound vibrations is the
questions.explanation: Sound-sensitive hair cells are in the cochlea.

questions.stem: Spectacles with convex lenses correct long-sightedness by
options: converging the light rays before they enter the eye
diverging the light rays before they enter the eye
reducing light intensity before it enters the eye
increasing light intensity before it enters the eye
questions.explanation: A converging lens brings the image forward onto the retina.

questions.stem: A seed of a flowering plant can best be described as
questions.explanation: A seed is a fertilised, developed ovule; the fruit is the developed ovary.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes removes carbon from the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis takes in CO2 from the air.

questions.stem: Which of the following cycles involves the process of precipitation and transpiration?
questions.explanation: Precipitation and transpiration are stages of the water cycle.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: What is the critical limiting factor for plants below the photic zone in an aquatic ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Below the photic zone too little light reaches for photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following instruments is used to estimate the number of plants in a habitat?
questions.explanation: Quadrats are used to count plants in sample areas.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about sandy soil? It
options: is light and easy to dig
questions.explanation: Sandy soil has large particles, is well aerated, drains fast and is light to dig.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of the following organisms is a primary consumer?
questions.explanation: The sheep feeds directly on plants (producers).

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: In the food chain P → Q → R → S → T, the organism designated P is normally sustained by energy from
questions.explanation: P is the producer, which traps energy from sunlight.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: In the food chain P → Q → R → S → T, which of the following statements best describes the organism designated R? It
options: is a producer as well as a consumer
questions.explanation: P is the producer, Q the primary consumer, so R (feeding on Q) is a secondary consumer.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases is not hereditary?
questions.explanation: Scabies is caused by a mite; the others are genetic.

questions.stem: The immediate product of meiosis in flowering plants is the
questions.explanation: Meiosis in the anther produces the pollen grains (microspores).

questions.stem: DNA in eukaryotic cells is contained in the
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic DNA is held in the nucleus.

questions.stem: Cytokinesis of mitosis is a process that ensures that
options: each daughter cell gets the necessary organelle
there is distribution of a complete set of genes into each daughter cell
daughter cells inherit new genetic combinations
worn out organelles are excluded from daughter cells
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is A because cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm and its organelles; the gene set is shared out by nuclear division (karyokinesis).

questions.topic: Structural, functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
questions.stem: An animal which is active during the day is known as a
questions.explanation: Day-active animals are diurnal.

questions.stem: Evidence of evolution includes the following except
questions.explanation: Mutation is a source of variation, not evidence of evolution.

questions.stem: A boy who is fond of swimming in a pond finds himself passing urine with traces of blood. He is likely to have contracted
questions.explanation: Urinary schistosomiasis (bilharzia), caught from snail-infested water, causes blood in urine.
